title: Tenant registry
requirement: The control plane shall keep a registry of tenants with a stable tenant identifier, display name, primary hostname and extra hostnames, region, status (Provisioning, Active, Suspended, ReadOnly, Decommissioned), plan, created and changed dates, and the location of the tenant database and object storage bucket.
rationale: Everything else resolves a request to a tenant through this registry.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new tenant record, When saved with a unique hostname, Then it is visible in the operator console and resolvable by hostname.|Given a hostname already used by another tenant, When saved, Then the save is refused. (error case)|Given a tenant in Suspended status, When any of its users call the API, Then the request is refused with a tenant-suspended message and no business code runs.
notes: Carried from the current product's per-tenant deployment list, now as data.

title: Automated tenant provisioning
requirement: The control plane shall provision a tenant with one job: create the tenant database from the current schema version, create the object storage bucket, seed reference data, create the first administrator with an invitation, register the hostname and write the tenant to the registry, finishing within 15 minutes and reporting each step.
rationale: Manual scripts are the largest operational risk found in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid tenant definition, When provisioning runs, Then the tenant is Active, the administrator receives an invitation and every step is logged with its duration.|Given a step fails (for example storage unavailable), When provisioning runs, Then the tenant stays in Provisioning, the failure is reported and the job can be resumed from the failed step. (error case)|Given provisioning is re-run for an Active tenant, When started, Then it is refused.
notes: Gap: today a runbook of manual steps.

title: Tenant resolution and context
requirement: Each tenant's deployment unit shall be bound to exactly one tenant from its configuration at start; the ingress shall route a tenant's hostnames to that unit only; the unit shall refuse any request whose hostname or token tenant claim does not match its tenant; its data layer shall hold credentials for that tenant's database only.
rationale: Isolation by construction, not by discipline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request on tenant A's unit with a token issued for tenant B, When processed, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a background job in tenant A's worker, When it runs, Then its queries run against tenant A's database only and its telemetry carries tenant A's identifier.|Given an unknown hostname, When requested at the ingress, Then a neutral error page is shown and no tenant unit receives the request.

title: Tenant lifecycle operations
requirement: An operator shall be able to suspend, reactivate, set read-only, rename, add or remove hostnames, change region (as a migration job) and decommission a tenant, each action audited and each status having defined behaviour for users.
rationale: Commercial and legal events (non-payment, contract end) need safe handling.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant set to ReadOnly, When a user tries a write, Then it is refused with a read-only message and reads still work.|Given a decommission request, When confirmed by a second operator, Then the tenant is frozen, a final export is produced, and data is deleted after the retention hold; a single operator cannot complete it. (error case)|Given a hostname removed, When a user opens it, Then the neutral error page is shown.

title: Tenant isolation guarantees
requirement: No operation shall be able to read or write another tenant's data: separate containers in separate namespaces with network policies, separate databases with separate database roles, separate buckets with separate credentials, separate secrets paths, separate caches and queues per unit, and an automated test suite that attempts cross-tenant access (network, database, storage, secrets) on every release.
rationale: The strongest promise a SaaS platform makes.
acceptance_criteria: Given the cross-tenant test suite, When run, Then zero cross-tenant reads or writes succeed.|Given a cache entry for tenant A, When tenant B asks for the same key, Then it misses.|Given a job queued for tenant A, When processed, Then it cannot resolve tenant B's connection. (error case)

title: Data residency
requirement: A tenant shall be assigned to one region at creation, all its data (database, files, backups, telemetry with content) shall stay in that region, and the region shall be shown in the tenant record and in contractual exports.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant in region X, When backups run, Then they are stored in region X only.|Given a request to move a tenant to region Y, When executed, Then it runs as a migration job with verification and the old copy is deleted after confirmation.|Given telemetry that contains request bodies, When exported, Then it goes to the regional telemetry backend only. (edge)|Given a request to store a tenant's backup outside its region, When attempted by any job, Then it is refused and alerted. (error case)

title: Tenant limits and quotas
requirement: The control plane shall hold per-tenant limits (users, storage, API requests per minute, jobs per hour, notification volume) with soft and hard thresholds, and the data plane shall enforce hard limits and raise alerts on soft limits.
rationale: Fair use and cost control in shared infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant at its hard API limit, When another request arrives, Then it is refused with a rate-limit response and a retry-after hint. (error case)|Given a tenant at 80% of storage, When measured, Then an alert and an in-console warning are raised.|Given limits changed by an operator, When saved, Then they apply within one minute without restart.

title: Usage metering
requirement: The platform shall meter per tenant per day: active users and assigned seats per module, API calls, storage, documents created per module (transactions, tracked for later pricing but not billed), notifications sent, jobs run, container resource use, and make the figures available to the operator console and billing.
rationale: Needed for per-user and transaction pricing and for capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria: Given a day of activity, When metering runs, Then figures are stored per tenant and day and match telemetry within 1%.|Given metering fails for a day, When detected, Then it is re-run from telemetry and the gap is closed. (error case)|Given a tenant exports usage, When requested, Then a file per month is produced.

title: Fleet health
requirement: The control plane shall show the health of every tenant (database reachable, migration version, last backup, job backlog, error rate, SLO status) and the version of every deployed component.
rationale: Running many tenants needs one view.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant behind on schema version, When the fleet view loads, Then it is flagged.|Given a tenant with a failed backup, When the view loads, Then it is flagged and an alert exists. (error case)|Given all tenants healthy, When the view loads, Then it shows green with the time of the last check.

title: Suites per tenant
requirement: The control plane shall record the suites each tenant has bought, one or more (ADR-0043), and the fleet shall install IronSaaS Foundation for every tenant and a suite only for the tenants that bought it: a suite's modules are migrated, seeded and loaded in those tenants' units and in no other. Adding a suite to an active tenant shall be an update job; removing one shall switch its modules off and keep its schemas, rows and files, so that adding it again finds them. Inside a suite, modules and features shall be entitlements (TF-040 to TF-046) with plans per suite: every tenant holds one Foundation plan, which names the business modules and the kernel's features (such as `authorization.role_transfer`), and one plan for each suite it bought, which names only that suite's modules and features; the tenant's entitlements are the union of its plans and reach the unit within a minute. One image per release carries the Foundation and every suite, and a unit loads its tenant's suites at start, from its configuration.
rationale: A customer buys the eProcurement Suite, or a later suite such as a School ERP, and rarely both. A unit that carried every suite would migrate schemas, run seeds and expose endpoints its tenant never bought, and what the system holds would grow with every suite. Plans per suite let each suite be sold on its own beside the Foundation every tenant has.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant provisioned with the eProcurement Suite, When provisioning finishes, Then the suite's schemas are migrated, its seeds have run, its endpoints answer, and its shell modules are listed for the people entitled to them.|Given a tenant provisioned without the eProcurement Suite, When its unit runs, Then its database holds none of the suite's schemas, the suite's endpoints answer not found, and the shell lists none of its modules.|Given an active tenant without the suite, When an operator adds the suite, Then an update job migrates, seeds and loads its modules, the tenant's suites in the control plane name it, and the change is audited with the operator.|Given an active tenant with the suite and records in it, When an operator removes the suite, Then its modules are switched off within a minute and its schemas, rows and files are kept; When the suite is added again, Then the same records are there.|Given a tenant with the suite, When an operator switches one of the suite's modules or features off in the tenant's plan for that suite, Then the unit and the shell follow within a minute, as for any entitlement (TF-040 to TF-046).|Given a tenant with a Foundation plan that includes `authorization.role_transfer` and a plan for the eProcurement Suite, When its entitlements are written to the store, Then they are the union of the two, and the Foundation's features apply whatever suites the tenant has.|Given a plan of the eProcurement Suite that names a module or feature of another suite or of the Foundation, When the plan is saved or applied, Then it is refused, naming the module or feature and the group it belongs to. (error case)
notes: New (ADR-0043, decided 2026-10-20). Scheduled with TF-241 in slice V, before the first suite slice (section 7). The tenant's suites live in Tenancy beside its plans; provisioning and the update job pass them into the unit's configuration; `make catalogue` already groups the licensable modules, features, flags and settings by suite, the Foundation first, which is what a plan of one group is checked against. Today's plans, Standard and Enterprise, become Foundation plans. Separate images per suite are a later option.

title: Accounts and principals
requirement: Identity shall manage principals of types User, ServiceAccount and ApiKey, each belonging to one tenant (or to the control plane), with a unique login identifier within the tenant, status (Invited, Active, Locked, Disabled), and profile attributes (name, email, phone, locale, timezone, avatar).
rationale: One model for everyone that can authenticate.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new user with a unique login identifier, When created, Then an invitation is sent and the status is Invited until the first login.|Given a duplicate login identifier in the same tenant, When created, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a Disabled principal, When it tries to authenticate, Then it is refused and all its sessions are revoked.
notes: Carried: user types Enterprise, Supplier, Platform, System, ServiceAccount become attributes, not separate code paths.

title: Password login
requirement: A user with a local credential shall log in with login identifier and password over TLS; passwords shall be hashed with a modern memory-hard algorithm (Argon2id) with per-user salt; failure messages shall not reveal whether the account exists.
acceptance_criteria: Given correct credentials, When submitted, Then a session is created and the user lands on the home page.|Given wrong credentials, When submitted, Then the message is "The login details are not correct" and the attempt is counted. (error case)|Given a stored password hash, When inspected, Then it is Argon2id with unique salt and the plain password is never logged.

title: Password policy, history and lockout
requirement: The platform shall enforce a tenant-configurable password policy (minimum length 12 by default, no common passwords by dictionary check, no reuse of the last 10, maximum age optional), lock an account for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts in 15 minutes, and notify the user of the lockout.
rationale: Gap: no policy or lockout exists in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a password in the common-password list, When set, Then it is refused with the reason.|Given 5 failures within 15 minutes, When the sixth attempt is made, Then it is refused with a locked message even with the correct password and an email is sent. (error case)|Given a reused password among the last 10, When set, Then it is refused.|Given a tenant administrator sets the minimum length, the history depth, the maximum age or the lockout's threshold, window or duration within its allowed range, When a password is next set or a sign-in next fails, Then the new value applies; a value outside its range is refused (ADR-0046).|Given a maximum age is set, When a user signs in with a password that has reached it, Then no session opens and the user sets a new password through a one-time link; in the 14 days before, the user is warned when the password expires.
notes: NIST 800-63B aligned: no forced periodic rotation by default.

title: Multi-factor authentication
requirement: The platform shall support time-based one-time codes (authenticator apps), passkeys (WebAuthn) and, as fallback, one-time codes by email or SMS; a tenant shall be able to require MFA for all users or for roles; recovery codes shall be issued at enrolment.
acceptance_criteria: Given MFA required for the tenant, When a user without a factor logs in, Then they are forced to enrol before reaching any page.|Given a wrong code three times, When the fourth is entered, Then a cooling period applies. (error case)|Given a lost device, When a recovery code is used, Then login succeeds, the code is consumed and the user is asked to enrol a new factor.
notes: Carried: current product has email OTP for password recovery and SMS OTP login for suppliers.

title: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect
requirement: A tenant shall be able to connect one or more OpenID Connect identity providers (discovery document, client credentials, claim mapping, allowed domains), mark users as SSO-only, and allow just-in-time user creation with a default role when the provider asserts an allowed domain.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configured provider and an allowed domain, When a new employee logs in through SSO, Then a user is created with the default role and a session starts.|Given an SSO-only user, When they try password login, Then it is refused with "Use your company login". (error case)|Given the provider returns an email outside allowed domains, When processed, Then login is refused and the attempt is audited.|Given a group claim mapped to a role at a scope, When a person signs in through the provider, Then they hold the role while the provider names them in the group, added and removed at each sign-in; a mapping can name only a role its author may grant at its scope (ADR-0031).|Given a provider whose ID token says multi-factor authentication was used, When the tenant trusts that provider's assertion, Then no second factor of this product is asked; otherwise the tenant's MFA policy applies as after a password (TF-013).|Given a provider's discovery address, When an administrator tests the connection, Then the discovery document and the signing keys are read and each check is reported in words as passed, a warning or failed.|Given an existing person whose email the provider has verified, When they first sign in through it, Then they are linked to it, the link is in their security activity and the audit trail, and later sign-ins find them by the provider's subject.|Given an email the provider has not marked verified, When processed, Then it matches and creates nobody, and the sign-in is refused and audited. (error case)|Given a deactivated person, When they sign in through a provider, Then the sign-in is refused and audited, and they are neither re-created nor reactivated. (error case)
notes: AC4 to AC9 added on 2026-10-22 (S3 T4, ADR-0048): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria.

title: Single sign-on with SAML 2.0
requirement: A tenant shall be able to connect a SAML 2.0 identity provider (metadata upload, signing certificate, attribute mapping) with the same user mapping rules as OpenID Connect.
acceptance_criteria: Given valid metadata, When saved, Then the service provider metadata is available for download.|Given an assertion with an invalid signature, When received, Then login is refused and audited. (error case)|Given certificate expiry within 30 days, When checked daily, Then administrators are warned.

title: Automatic user provisioning (SCIM 2.0)
requirement: A tenant shall be able to enable SCIM 2.0 so that its identity provider creates, updates, deactivates users and syncs group membership to roles, authenticated by a dedicated bearer token with rotation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a SCIM create, When received, Then a user exists in Invited or Active status per configuration.|Given a SCIM deactivate, When received, Then the user is Disabled within one minute and sessions are revoked.|Given an invalid token, When received, Then the request is refused and counted. (error case)

title: Password recovery and change
requirement: A user shall recover a password through a one-time link or code sent to the verified email (valid 15 minutes, single use), and change a password by providing the current one; both actions are audited and end other sessions when the user chooses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid recovery code within 15 minutes, When used, Then the password can be set once and the code is consumed.|Given a code used twice, When the second attempt is made, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a password change, When saved, Then the user may end all other sessions in the same step.|Given a password change, When the current password given is wrong, Then the change is refused and the attempt counts towards the lockout like a failed sign-in. (error case)

title: User invitations
requirement: Administrators shall invite users by email with a signed, time-limited link (default 72 hours, resendable), and the invitee shall set credentials (or complete SSO) and accept terms before activation.
rationale: Carried from supplier invitation; generalised for all users.
acceptance_criteria: Given an invitation, When accepted within the window, Then the account becomes Active.|Given an expired link, When opened, Then an expiry page with a request-new-link action is shown and nothing changes. (error case)|Given an invitation resent, When sent, Then the previous link is invalid.

title: Account security events to the user
requirement: The platform shall email the user on new device login, password change, MFA change, lockout and impersonation of their account, with a link to review sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a login from a new device, When completed, Then a notification is sent within one minute.|Given the user opens the link, When loaded, Then active sessions are listed with end-session actions.|Given notifications fail to send, When detected, Then the event is still audited. (error case)

title: Step-up re-authentication
requirement: A high-risk action shall need a recent authentication: the person proved who they are within the minutes the action declares, five unless it says otherwise. When the last authentication is older, the action is refused, nothing changes, and the shell asks the person to confirm it is them in one shared dialog: their password, and their second factor when they have one (TF-013). The action is then sent again. A session's authentication is its sign-in or its latest confirmation; a bearer token's is its issue. The first actions behind it are issuing a recovery link, resetting someone's second factors, deactivating a person, granting a role that holds a high-risk or critical permission, and changing the MFA policy; break-glass access, electronic signatures and second approvals use the same mechanism when they come.
rationale: An open session, left unattended or taken over, should not be enough to change who can do what. Asking again at the moment of the action limits what a stolen session can do without asking at every request.
acceptance_criteria: Given a person who last authenticated more than five minutes ago, When they issue a recovery link, reset someone's factors, deactivate a person, grant a role with a high-risk or critical permission, or change the MFA policy, Then the action is refused as needing a recent authentication and nothing changes. (error case)|Given that refusal, When the person confirms their password and, when they have one, their second factor, Then the same action succeeds, and the confirmation is audited.|Given a person who authenticated within the last five minutes, When they take one of these actions, Then it goes on without asking again.|Given a wrong password or a wrong second factor in the confirmation, When it is sent, Then the action stays refused, the failure counts towards the lockout and the cooling period as at sign-in, and the session stays open. (error case)|Given an action the API refuses for an old authentication, When the shell receives the refusal, Then the shared dialog opens and, once the person has confirmed, the action is sent again without the person repeating it.|Given a person who signs in through a company login and has no password, When they confirm it is them, Then their provider is asked for a fresh sign-in (`prompt=login` and `max_age=0`), after their second factor here when they have one, and the confirmation counts only when the ID token's `auth_time` falls within the step-up window; otherwise it fails with a message that the company login did not ask for a new sign-in, the action stays refused, and either way the person returns to the page they were on, with the action ready to redo (ADR-0048).
notes: New 2026-10-22 (S3 T3, ADR-0047); AC6 added at S3 T4's review, the same day. The API declares it on an endpoint (`RequireRecentAuthentication(minutes)`) or asks for it in a service where the rule depends on the data, a role's permissions or a setting's key; both ask one kernel interface. A token's client gets a fresh token with its credentials.

title: Sessions and tokens
requirement: UI logins shall create a server-side session referenced by a secure, same-site cookie; API clients shall receive short-lived access tokens (15 minutes) and rotating refresh tokens (reuse detection revokes the family); tokens shall be signed with keys from the secrets store and validated for issuer, audience, lifetime and signature with zero clock skew.
rationale: Carried and hardened from the current token model.
acceptance_criteria: Given a refresh token used twice, When the second use is detected, Then the whole token family is revoked and the user is notified. (error case)|Given an access token older than 15 minutes, When used, Then it is refused and the client refreshes.|Given a signing key rotation, When performed, Then tokens signed with the previous key stay valid until their expiry and new tokens use the new key.

title: Session inactivity and limits
requirement: A session shall end after a tenant-configurable inactivity period (default 60 minutes) and an absolute maximum (default 12 hours); a tenant may limit concurrent sessions per user; the UI shall warn before expiry and offer to continue.
rationale: Carried from the current product; adds absolute maximum.
acceptance_criteria: Given 60 minutes without activity, When the next request arrives, Then it is refused with a session-expired signal and the UI returns to login. (error case)|Given a limit of one concurrent session, When a second login happens, Then the first session is ended and the user informed. (edge)|Given a session at 12 hours, When active, Then it ends and re-authentication is required.

title: Session management console
requirement: Users shall see and end their own sessions (device, approximate location, start, last activity); tenant administrators with the permission shall see and end any session, see concurrent users and a daily summary; all ends are audited with reason.
acceptance_criteria: Given an administrator ends a session, When the user makes a request, Then it is refused and the audit shows who ended it and why.|Given a user without the permission, When opening all sessions, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given no active sessions, When listed, Then an empty state is shown.|Given a person signed in on several devices, When they open their sessions, Then each shows the browser and platform, the city and country, when it started and was last used, and how it signed in; they can end any but the one they use, or all the others at once.|Given an administrator with the permission, When they open the sessions console, Then it shows how many people are signed in now and, for each recent day, the sessions started, the most people signed in at once, and the sessions an administrator ended.
notes: AC4 and AC5 added on 2026-10-22 (S3 T5, ADR-0049): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria.

title: Service accounts and client credentials
requirement: A tenant administrator shall create service accounts with a client identifier and a secret shown once (stored hashed), bound to roles whose scope is "service", with optional IP allow-list and expiry; service accounts authenticate with the client-credentials flow and never through the UI.
acceptance_criteria: Given valid credentials, When a token is requested, Then it carries the service account's permissions and the tenant claim.|Given a request from an IP outside the allow-list, When made, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given secret rotation, When performed, Then both old and new secrets work for a configurable overlap (default 24 hours), then only the new one.

title: API keys for simple integrations
requirement: A tenant administrator shall issue API keys bound to a service account and a reduced permission set, with expiry and last-used tracking, for integrations that cannot run an OAuth flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid key, When used, Then the request runs with the key's permissions only.|Given an expired key, When used, Then it is refused and the owner is notified. (error case)|Given a key unused for 90 days, When reviewed, Then it is flagged in the console.

title: Impersonation with attribution
requirement: A principal with the impersonation permission shall start an impersonation session for a user of the same tenant (or, for operators, of any tenant) with a mandatory reason; every action shall record both the acting user and the impersonator; the impersonated user shall be notified; impersonation shall end automatically after a maximum duration (default 2 hours).
rationale: Carried from the current product; adds reason and time limit.
acceptance_criteria: Given an impersonation start without reason, When submitted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a change made during impersonation, When audited, Then actor and impersonator are both recorded.|Given 2 hours pass, When the next request arrives, Then the impersonation ends and the impersonator returns to their own session.|Given a person who holds a permission the impersonator does not, When the impersonator starts an impersonation of them, Then it is refused, as a recovery link would be (ADR-0046). (error case)|Given an impersonation, When the impersonator confirms it is them, signs, approves as the second person, or changes the person's factors, password or sessions, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an impersonation, When the person impersonated opens their security activity, Then it shows who signed in as them, when, and why.
notes: AC4 to AC6 added on 2026-10-22 (S3 T5, ADR-0049): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria. The email to the person impersonated waits for S4's notifications.

title: Break-glass access
requirement: Operators shall have an emergency access path to a tenant that requires two operators, a ticket reference and a time limit, grants a predefined role, records every action and raises a review task when it ends.
rationale: Incidents happen; uncontrolled admin access is worse.
acceptance_criteria: Given one operator requests break-glass, When the second approves with a ticket reference, Then access is granted for the time limit.|Given no second approval within 30 minutes, When checked, Then the request expires. (error case)|Given access ends, When processed, Then a review task with the full action list is created.|Given the operator who requested break-glass, When they approve their own request, Then it is refused: the second operator is someone else. (error case)
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-22 (S3 T5, ADR-0049). Until S5's task engine the review is a record in the control plane and an event in the tenant's audit trail.

title: Device and login risk signals
requirement: The platform shall record device fingerprint, IP and approximate location per login, flag impossible travel and new countries, and allow a tenant to require MFA step-up on risky logins.
acceptance_criteria: Given a login from a new country, When evaluated, Then MFA step-up is required when the tenant setting is on.|Given two logins 1,000 km apart within 10 minutes, When evaluated, Then the second is flagged and the user notified.|Given location lookup unavailable, When logging in, Then login still works and the flag is skipped. (error case)

title: Consent and terms acceptance
requirement: The platform shall record acceptance of terms, privacy notice and tenant-specific documents (version, time, principal) and require re-acceptance when a document version changes.
rationale: Carried from supplier NDA and terms signing; generalised.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new terms version, When a user logs in, Then they must accept before continuing.|Given acceptance, When recorded, Then version, time and identity are stored and visible to administrators.|Given a service account, When authenticating, Then no acceptance is required. (edge)|Given a user who declines the new terms, When they try to continue, Then access is refused until acceptance. (error case)

title: Logout and revocation
requirement: Logout shall end the session server-side and clear the cookie; administrators shall be able to revoke all sessions and tokens of a user, a service account or the whole tenant (for example after an incident).
rationale: Revocation must be immediate, not at token expiry.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant-wide revocation, When executed, Then every session and refresh token is invalid within one minute.|Given a revoked access token still within its 15 minutes, When used on a sensitive operation, Then it is refused because the session check runs on every request. (error case)|Given logout, When the back button is used, Then no protected page is served. (edge)|Given an administrator revokes everything of a person or a service account with a reason, When their sessions or tokens are used, Then they are refused, and the audit trail and the person's security activity say who did it and why.
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-22 (S3 T5, ADR-0049): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria.

title: Permission catalogue
requirement: Every module shall declare its permissions in code as `module.resource.action` with a description and risk level; the catalogue shall be registered at start-up and exposed to the role editor; an operation without a declared permission (or an explicit anonymous marker) shall fail the start-up check.
rationale: Gap: 242 unguarded operations in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given an operation registered without a permission or anonymous marker, When the host starts, Then start-up fails with the operation named. (error case)|Given a new module, When registered, Then its permissions appear in the role editor grouped by module and, within a module, by resource.|Given the anonymous allow-list, When reviewed, Then it contains only login, recovery, invitation acceptance, public branding and health.|Given a permission declared with a name outside the form `module.resource.action` or without a description, When declared, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Carried: 287 permissions and their naming pattern.

title: Permission enforcement on every operation
requirement: The API shall check the declared permission before any business code runs, return a forbidden response with a stable error code when missing, and log the denial with principal, operation and tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Given a principal without the permission, When calling, Then the response is forbidden and an audit event records the denial.|Given a permission granted one second ago, When calling, Then it works without re-login (permissions are loaded per request or cached for at most 60 seconds).|Given an anonymous operation, When called without a token, Then it works and nothing tenant-specific is exposed. (edge)|Given a permission check that fails because the catalogue is unavailable, When evaluated, Then access is denied (fail closed) and an alert is raised. (error case)

title: Roles
requirement: A tenant administrator shall create roles as named sets of permissions, scoped to a principal type (user or service), with system roles that cannot be edited (Tenant Administrator, Read Only, Service Default) and tenant roles that can; roles shall be exportable and importable between tenants.
rationale: Carried; adds system roles and portability.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant role with permissions, When assigned, Then the principal's effective permissions include them on the next request.|Given an attempt to edit a system role, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a role export, When imported into another tenant, Then unknown permissions are reported in the dry run and refuse the apply (ADR-0031).|Given a tenant administrator, When they create a tenant role, change its name, description or permissions, and delete it, Then each change is saved and read back, and the deleted role is gone.|Given a tenant role created, changed or deleted, When audited, Then the event holds the role's permissions before and after the change.|Given the roles of one tenant exported, When imported into another, Then a dry run lists what would be created and changed and changes nothing, and the apply creates the roles with the same permissions and audits each.

title: Role assignments with scope
requirement: A role shall be assigned to a principal for a scope: the whole tenant, an organisation unit (and optionally its children), or a specific record type and record; effective permissions shall be evaluated for the scope of the record being accessed.
rationale: Enterprises need buyers for one legal entity, approvers for one business unit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a role assigned for organisation unit A, When the principal accesses a record of unit B, Then it answers not found, as for a record that does not exist (ADR-0031, ADR-0032).|Given a role assigned for the tenant, When any record is accessed, Then the permission applies.|Given an assignment with children included, When a record of a child unit is accessed, Then the permission applies. (edge)|Given an assignment to a scope that does not exist, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an administrator, When they grant a role to a principal at a unit with its children, list the assignments of the principal and of the unit, and remove the grant, Then the grant is listed with its role and scope, and after the removal it is gone.

title: Organisation units
requirement: Each tenant shall have an organisation unit tree (legal entities, business units, departments, teams) maintained by administrators, used for role scope, settings overrides and data visibility; a principal belongs to one home unit and may be granted access to others.
rationale: One structure for scoping across modules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a unit moved under another parent, When saved, Then scoped assignments follow it.|Given a unit with children, When deleted, Then it is refused until children are moved. (error case)|Given a user with home unit A, When listing records, Then the default filter is unit A and its children.|Given a parent unit, When an administrator creates a unit under it, Then the unit takes its path under the parent and the creation is audited.|Given a unit's code, When saved, Then it holds lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, is stored in lowercase and is unique in the tenant, and any other code is refused on its field. (error case)|Given a unit renamed, When saved, Then the audit records the old and the new name.|Given a parent unit, When a child of a kind the parent may not hold is created, Then it is refused on its field. (error case)|Given the tree, When it is read, Then the units come depth first from the root, siblings by name.
notes: Carried: content groups, legal entities and departments become one tree.

title: Record-level policies
requirement: Modules shall declare record-level policies (owner can edit while draft; supplier users see only their supplier's records; approvers see records they must approve; unit visibility) through a small policy interface evaluated by the service for reads by identifier and applied as filters for lists; policies shall be unit-tested per module.
rationale: Gap: supplier operations without ownership checks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier user requesting another supplier's order by identifier, When evaluated, Then it answers not found (ADR-0032). (error case)|Given a list request, When executed, Then the policy filter is part of the query so paging counts are correct.|Given a record with no policy declared, When accessed, Then the build check fails for that module.

title: Segregation of duties rules
requirement: A tenant administrator shall define conflict rules between permissions or roles (for example create supplier and approve supplier), and the platform shall block or warn on assignments that create conflicts and report existing conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Given a blocking rule, When a conflicting role is assigned, Then it is refused with the rule named. (error case)|Given a warning rule, When assigned, Then it is allowed and listed in the conflicts report.|Given rules changed, When the report runs, Then existing conflicts appear within one day.

title: Delegation of duties
requirement: A user (or an administrator on their behalf) shall delegate specific duties (approval, receiving, evaluation, or all) to another user for a date range with a reason; the delegate acts with the delegator's rights for those duties, actions record both identities, and overlapping or circular delegations are refused.
rationale: Carried from the current product, including its four overlap rules.
acceptance_criteria: Given an active approval delegation, When a workflow assigns the delegator, Then the delegate is also assigned and may act.|Given a circular delegation (A to B while B to A in the same period), When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a delegate acts, When audited, Then the entry names the delegate and the delegator.

title: Access reviews
requirement: The platform shall support periodic access reviews: a campaign lists principals and their roles per unit, reviewers confirm or revoke, decisions are recorded and overdue reviews escalate.
acceptance_criteria: Given a campaign started, When reviewers open it, Then they see only their units' principals.|Given a revoke decision, When recorded, Then the assignment ends immediately.|Given a review overdue by 7 days, When checked, Then the reviewer's manager is notified. (edge)|Given a reviewer who is not the owner of the unit, When they try to decide, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Effective access explanation
requirement: An administrator shall be able to ask "why can (or cannot) this principal perform this action on this record" and receive the roles, scopes, policies, entitlements and flags that led to the decision.
acceptance_criteria: Given a denied action, When explained, Then the first failing check is named.|Given an allowed action, When explained, Then the granting role and scope are named.|Given a principal from another tenant, When explained, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Module and feature entitlements
requirement: The control plane shall hold per tenant the licensed modules and features with status (Enabled, Disabled, ReadOnly, Expired), subscription dates, user limits and subscription type (per user, per transaction, platform); the data plane shall hide and refuse operations of modules not enabled and make ReadOnly modules read-only.
acceptance_criteria: Given a module Disabled, When a user opens the application, Then its menu is absent and its operations are refused.|Given a module in ReadOnly, When a write is attempted, Then it is refused with a read-only message and reads work. (error case)|Given a subscription end date passed, When evaluated, Then the status is Expired and treated as Disabled with a grace period configurable per plan. (edge)

title: Per-user entitlements and seats
requirement: For per-user modules, administrators shall assign seats to users within the licensed count; the platform shall refuse assignments above the count and report seat usage.
acceptance_criteria: Given 50 seats with 50 assigned, When a 51st is assigned, Then it is refused with the count shown. (error case)|Given a seat removed, When done, Then the user loses the module on the next request.|Given seat usage, When viewed, Then assigned and remaining are shown per module.

title: Plans and plan templates
requirement: The control plane shall define plans as templates of modules, features, limits and flags, and apply a plan to a tenant in one action with differences shown before confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a plan applied, When confirmed, Then entitlements and limits match the plan and the change is audited.|Given a plan change that removes a module in use, When previewed, Then a warning lists affected data.|Given a plan with an unknown feature, When applied, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Entitlement checks in UI and API
requirement: Both the UI shell and the API shall evaluate entitlements from one effective-entitlement service with a cache of at most 60 seconds, so that a change in the control plane is visible everywhere within a minute.
rationale: One source of truth, no drift between surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Given a module enabled, When 60 seconds pass, Then the menu appears without re-login.|Given a UI that still shows a disabled module, When an operation is called, Then the API refuses it regardless of the UI. (error case)|Given the control plane unreachable, When evaluating, Then the last known entitlements are used for up to 24 hours and an alert is raised. (edge)

title: Trial and grace periods
requirement: A module may be in Trial with an end date and a user limit, and in Grace after expiry for a configurable number of days with warnings shown to administrators.
acceptance_criteria: Given a trial ending in 7 days, When administrators log in, Then a banner shows the date.|Given grace ended, When evaluated, Then the module is Disabled.|Given a trial converted, When confirmed, Then dates and status update without data change. (edge)|Given a trial extension beyond the operator maximum, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Entitlement audit and history
requirement: Every entitlement change shall be audited with operator, time, before and after values, and a tenant's entitlement history shall be viewable.
acceptance_criteria: Given a change, When audited, Then before and after are stored.|Given history requested, When viewed, Then changes are listed in order with operator.|Given an attempt to edit history, When made, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Feature-level entitlements
requirement: Within a module, features (for example advanced matching, auctions pre-bidding) shall be entitleable separately and checkable by product code through the same service.
acceptance_criteria: Given a feature disabled, When its operation is called, Then it is refused with a not-entitled code. (error case)|Given a feature enabled, When the UI loads, Then the related controls appear.|Given a feature of a disabled module, When enabled alone, Then it is still unavailable because the module governs. (edge)

title: Feature flags with scopes
requirement: The platform shall provide feature flags of types boolean, string, number and JSON, with rules by scope: global, region, tenant, organisation unit, user, percentage rollout and attribute match; flags shall be evaluated through the OpenFeature SDK in both UI and API with the tenant and user context.
rationale: Release behaviour without deploys; separate from commercial entitlements.
acceptance_criteria: Given a flag on for 10% of tenants, When evaluated, Then the same tenant always gets the same result (stable hashing).|Given a flag off globally but on for tenant A, When evaluated for A, Then it is on.|Given the flag service unavailable, When evaluated, Then the last known value is used; the default value in code is used only when no value was ever known, and then an alert is raised (ADR-0035). (error case)
notes: Gap: no flags in the current product.

title: Kill switches
requirement: Critical paths (outbound email, webhooks, SMS, AI service calls, live push, imports) shall each have a kill switch flag that stops the path within one minute and shows a banner to administrators.
acceptance_criteria: Given the email kill switch on, When notifications are processed, Then emails are marked Blocked and other channels continue.|Given the switch off again, When processed, Then blocked emails are retried.|Given a switch flipped, When audited, Then operator, time and reason are recorded.|Given a non-operator tries to flip a kill switch, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Flag lifecycle
requirement: Each flag shall have an owner, a purpose, a type (release, experiment, operational, permission-like), a planned removal date and a status; flags past their removal date shall be reported; removing a flag from code with rules still defined shall fail the build.
acceptance_criteria: Given a flag past removal date, When the weekly report runs, Then it lists the flag and owner.|Given a flag deleted in code but defined in the registry, When the build runs, Then it fails with the flag named. (error case)|Given a flag created, When saved without owner, Then it is refused.

title: Flag evaluation audit and exposure
requirement: Flag rule changes shall be audited; evaluations for experiments shall record exposure events (flag, variant, principal, time) for analysis without storing personal data beyond the principal identifier.
rationale: Experiments need evidence; changes need traceability.
acceptance_criteria: Given a rule change, When saved, Then operator, before and after are audited.|Given an experiment flag, When evaluated for a user the first time, Then one exposure event is recorded.|Given exposure recording fails, When evaluating, Then the value is still returned. (error case)

title: Flags in the UI shell
requirement: The shell shall receive the evaluated flags for the current user at login and on change, expose them to product UIs through one hook, and never trust UI flags for security decisions.
rationale: One way for product UIs to use flags.
acceptance_criteria: Given a flag changes, When the shell polls or receives a push, Then components re-render within one minute.|Given a flag-hidden control, When its API is called directly, Then the API applies its own evaluation. (edge)|Given the flag list fails to load, When the shell starts, Then defaults apply and the shell still works. (error case)

title: Tenant-visible flags
requirement: Some flags shall be marked tenant-visible so that a tenant administrator can switch them in the tenant console (for example enable beta features) within limits set by the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant-visible flag, When the tenant administrator switches it, Then it applies to that tenant only.|Given a flag not tenant-visible, When the tenant console is used, Then it is not shown.|Given an operator limit (for example maximum 10% of users), When the tenant exceeds it, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Flag provider portability
requirement: The flag provider shall be replaceable (in-house database provider by default; Unleash or others later) without changes to product code, through the OpenFeature provider interface.
acceptance_criteria: Given the provider swapped, When the application starts, Then all evaluations work with the same keys.|Given a provider misconfiguration, When starting, Then start-up fails with a clear message. (error case)|Given both providers configured, When evaluating, Then the configured primary wins. (edge)

title: Typed settings with hierarchy
requirement: Modules shall declare settings in code with key, type (text, number, boolean, choice, JSON, secret reference), default, validation rule, scope levels allowed (system, tenant, organisation unit, user) and a description; values shall be resolved by the hierarchy user, unit (walking up the tree), tenant, system default, with one effective-value service and a cache of at most 60 seconds.
rationale: Carried: 84 keys in the current product, now typed and scoped.
acceptance_criteria: Given a setting overridden at unit level, When a user of a child unit asks for it, Then the unit value applies over the tenant value.|Given a value that fails validation, When saved, Then it is refused with the rule shown. (error case)|Given a secret-type setting, When read by the UI, Then only a reference is returned, never the value.

title: Settings administration and audit
requirement: The tenant console shall show settings grouped by module and scope with descriptions, defaults, who changed what and when, and allow reset to default; every change shall be audited with before and after values.
acceptance_criteria: Given a change, When saved, Then the audit shows old, new, actor and time.|Given reset to default, When confirmed, Then the override is removed and the inherited value is shown.|Given a user without the settings permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Settings exposure to products and UI
requirement: Product code shall read settings through a typed accessor generated from the declarations; the UI shall receive the effective non-secret settings for the current user; settings changes shall apply without restart.
acceptance_criteria: Given a setting key not declared, When read in code, Then it fails compilation (typed accessor).|Given a setting changed, When 60 seconds pass, Then new reads return the new value without restart.|Given a secret reference setting, When product code reads it, Then the secret is fetched from the secrets store at that moment and never cached longer than 5 minutes. (edge)|Given a settings cache that cannot be refreshed, When read, Then the last value is used and an alert is raised after 5 minutes. (error case)

title: Append-only audit log
requirement: The platform shall write an audit event for every authentication event, permission denial, role or entitlement or setting or flag change, status change of a business record, approval decision, impersonation, data export and administrative action, with: event type, time (UTC, server clock), tenant, actor, impersonator, principal type, record type and identifier, summary, before and after values where applicable, reason where given, correlation id and source (UI, API, job); audit rows shall never be updated or deleted.
rationale: Gap: uneven coverage and unprotected rows in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given any status change of a business record, When committed, Then an audit event exists in the same transaction.|Given an attempt to update or delete an audit row (even by a database administrator role used by the application), When made, Then it is refused by database permissions. (error case)|Given a job acting on behalf of the system, When audited, Then actor is the system principal and source is job.

title: Audit integrity chain
requirement: Audit events shall be hash-chained per tenant (each event stores the hash of the previous event and of its own content); a daily job shall verify the chain and alert on any gap or mismatch; chain anchors shall be stored outside the tenant database.
acceptance_criteria: Given the daily verification, When the chain is intact, Then a verification record is stored.|Given a modified row, When verified, Then the mismatch is reported with the event identifier and an alert is raised. (error case)|Given a restored backup, When verified, Then the anchor comparison shows the restore point.

title: Change history (field level)
requirement: For every entity marked as tracked, the platform shall record field-level changes (field, old value, new value) grouped per save, with actor, impersonator, time and reason, and show them on the record; tracking shall be declared per entity and the build shall fail when a business document entity is not tracked.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tracked entity changed in two fields, When saved, Then one history group with two detail rows exists.|Given a business document entity without the tracked marker, When the build runs, Then it fails naming the entity. (error case)|Given a secret or sensitive field (bank account), When changed, Then history stores a masked value.|Given a save of a tracked record, When its history is written, Then it is an audit event in the trail's hash chain, in the save's own transaction, and a save whose history cannot be written is not saved (ADR-0051).
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-23 (S3 T7, ADR-0051): the history is part of the audit trail, not beside it.

title: Electronic signatures
requirement: Approval decisions, acknowledgements and document signings shall be recorded as electronic signatures: signer identity, authentication method used, time, meaning (approved, rejected, acknowledged, signed), record type, identifier and version hash, optional signature image; a tenant may require re-authentication (password or MFA) at signing for selected document types.
rationale: 21 CFR Part 11 and similar regimes; carried from supplier NDA signing.
acceptance_criteria: Given re-authentication required, When an approver approves without it, Then the action is refused until re-authentication. (error case)|Given a signature, When viewed, Then signer, time, meaning and record version are shown and the record content hash matches.|Given a record changed after signing, When viewed, Then the signature is shown as applying to the earlier version.|Given a person's first signature in a session, When they sign, Then it asks for their login identifier, their password and their second factor when they have one; a later signature in the same session asks for their password, and for the second factor only when the tenant requires it; a session that ended, by sign-out or the idle limit, starts again at the first rule (21 CFR 11.200, ADR-0051).|Given a person who signs in through their company login, When they sign, Then each signature needs a fresh sign-in at the provider within the step-up window, taken by that signature only (ADR-0048, ADR-0051).|Given someone signed in as another person, acting for another person, or a token or service account, When they try to sign, Then the signature is refused whatever the credentials and the attempt is recorded in the audit trail. (error case) (ADR-0049, ADR-0051)
notes: AC4 to AC6 added on 2026-10-23 (S3 T7, ADR-0051): the tests prove Part 11's components rule and who may never sign, beyond the first three criteria. Meanings: approved, rejected, acknowledged, signed and reviewed.

title: Audit search, export and retention
requirement: Permitted users shall search audit events by time, actor, record and type, export results to CSV, and the platform shall retain audit events for a tenant-configurable period (default 7 years) with archival to object storage after a configurable online period.
rationale: Auditors need access; storage needs control.
acceptance_criteria: Given a search by record, When run, Then all events for the record appear in time order.|Given events older than the online period, When archived, Then they remain searchable by date range through the archive index.|Given a user without the audit permission, When searching, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an audit event of any type, When shown in the audit trail, a record's History tab or an export, Then its type reads as words; the build fails for an event type no module names (ADR-0051).

title: Time source
requirement: All servers shall synchronise time by NTP; timestamps shall be stored in UTC; displays shall use the user's timezone with the zone named; audit and workflow shall never accept client-supplied timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client sends a timestamp, When a record is created, Then the server time is stored.|Given a user in another zone, When viewing, Then the zone is shown with the time.|Given NTP drift above 1 second, When detected, Then an alert is raised. (error case)

title: Data retention and legal hold
requirement: Retention policies per record type (business documents 7 years after closure by default; notifications 12 months; sessions 12 months; telemetry 30 days online) shall be configurable per tenant within operator limits, applied by jobs that archive then delete, and overridden by legal holds that stop deletion for named records or the whole tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record past retention, When the job runs, Then it is archived and then deleted with an audit event.|Given a legal hold on a supplier, When the job runs, Then its records are skipped.|Given a tenant tries to set retention below the operator minimum, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Compliance evidence exports
requirement: The platform shall produce evidence packs on demand: user access list with roles, admin actions in a period, security settings snapshot, audit chain verification results, backup and restore drill records.
rationale: Audits (SOC 2, ISO 27001, customer audits) ask for the same artefacts repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a period, When the pack is generated, Then it contains the five documents with the tenant and time range.|Given a pack generated, When audited, Then the export is recorded with requester.|Given a user without the compliance permission, When requesting, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Approval of sensitive configuration changes
requirement: A tenant may require a second administrator to approve changes to selected configuration areas (roles, SSO, retention, entitlements) before they apply.
acceptance_criteria: Given four-eyes enabled for roles, When an administrator saves a role, Then it is pending until another administrator approves.|Given the same administrator tries to approve, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given approval, When done, Then the change applies and both identities are audited.

title: Operational logs separate from audit
requirement: Operational logs (debug, errors, performance) shall be separate from audit events, shall never be the only record of a business action, and shall not contain personal data beyond identifiers (scrubbing enricher).
acceptance_criteria: Given an error log entry, When inspected, Then it contains identifiers but no names, emails or document content.|Given a business action, When logs are deleted after 30 days, Then its audit event still exists.|Given a developer writes a personal field to the log, When the scrubber runs, Then it is masked. (edge)|Given a developer tries to delete an audit event through the operational log tools, When attempted, Then it is refused because audit storage is separate. (error case)

title: Secure defaults for the web surface
requirement: Every response shall carry security headers (content security policy without unsafe inline, strict transport security, frame denial, content type options, referrer policy, permissions policy); cookies shall be Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite; cross-origin access shall be allowed only for configured origins per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Given any response, When inspected, Then all headers are present with the configured values.|Given a request from an origin not configured, When made from a browser, Then it is blocked by CORS. (error case)|Given an inline script in a product UI, When the CSP applies, Then it is blocked and reported to the CSP report endpoint.|Given any cookie the platform sets, When inspected, Then it is Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-27 (S3 T9a, ADR-0053): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria.

title: Input validation and output encoding
requirement: All inputs shall be validated by declared schemas (type, length, range, pattern, allowed values) before reaching services; HTML shall be sanitised where rich text is allowed; file names and paths shall be normalised; all output shall be encoded by the UI framework; database access shall be parameterised only.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request with a field over its length, When received, Then a validation problem names the field.|Given rich text with a script tag, When saved, Then the tag is removed and the rest kept.|Given a dynamic query built by string concatenation, When the code scan runs, Then it fails the build. (error case)|Given a file name with path parts, control characters or more than its length, When the file is stored, Then it is kept under a key the platform makes, and its name, cleaned and shortened, only as display text.|Given a page of the shell that sets HTML from a string, When the lint runs, Then it fails, unless it is the one component that shows sanitised rich text. (error case)
notes: Carried: the current product blocks script tags with a middleware; now validation by schema. AC4 and AC5 added on 2026-10-27 (S3 T9a, ADR-0053): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria.

title: Rate limiting and anti-automation
requirement: The platform shall apply rate limits per IP, per principal and per tenant with sensible defaults (login 10 per minute per IP, password recovery 5 per hour per account, API 600 per minute per principal, exports 20 per hour), return retry-after hints, and apply progressive delays and CAPTCHA (self-hosted, open source) on login after repeated failures.
rationale: Gap: no rate limiting in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given 11 login attempts in a minute from one IP, When the 11th arrives, Then it is refused with retry-after.|Given a principal at its API limit, When another call arrives, Then it is refused and the event counted. (error case)|Given limits changed for a tenant, When saved, Then they apply within one minute.|Given 5 failed sign-ins within 15 minutes from one address or for one login identifier, When the next sign-in is made, Then it needs a solved proof-of-work challenge that the platform serves itself and checks once, and each further failure from the address makes the next challenge's work larger. (error case)
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-27 (S3 T9a, ADR-0053): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria; the progressive delay is the challenge's work.

title: Secrets management
requirement: All secrets (database credentials, signing keys, provider keys, client secrets) shall live in the secrets store, be fetched at start and on rotation, never be written to logs, configuration files or the repository; the repository shall be scanned for secrets on every change and the build shall fail on a finding.
rationale: Gap: a live credential in a readme in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a secret in a committed file, When the pipeline runs, Then it fails naming the file and the secret type. (error case)|Given a rotated database credential, When the application reloads secrets, Then connections use the new credential without restart.|Given an exception that contains a connection string, When logged, Then the secret is masked.

title: Encryption at rest and in transit
requirement: All traffic shall use TLS 1.2 or higher with modern ciphers; databases, backups and object storage shall be encrypted at rest; selected fields (bank accounts, tax identifiers, personal identifiers) shall be encrypted at the application level with tenant-specific keys and searchable only by exact match through a keyed hash.
acceptance_criteria: Given a database dump, When inspected, Then application-encrypted fields are unreadable.|Given a search by exact tax identifier, When run, Then the record is found through the keyed hash.|Given a TLS 1.0 client, When connecting, Then the connection is refused. (error case)|Given a search by a part of an encrypted field's value, When run, Then nothing is found: only the exact value finds the record. (error case)|Given a tenant's unit, When it uses another tenant's key, Then the key service refuses it. (error case)
notes: AC4 and AC5 added on 2026-10-28 (S3 T9b, ADR-0054): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first three criteria, the search only by exact match and the tenant-specific keys.

title: Key management and rotation
requirement: Encryption and signing keys shall be versioned, rotated on a schedule (signing yearly, data keys per policy) and on demand, with re-encryption jobs for data keys and overlap periods for signing keys; key operations shall be audited.
acceptance_criteria: Given a data key rotated, When the re-encryption job finishes, Then all values use the new key version and the old key is retired.|Given a signing key rotated, When old tokens arrive, Then they validate until expiry.|Given a key operation, When performed, Then it is audited with operator and reason.|Given a rotation attempted without the key officer permission, When requested, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a key whose scheduled rotation is due, When the schedule runs, Then the key is rotated and the rotation audited as an operator's would be.
notes: AC5 added on 2026-10-28 (S3 T9b, ADR-0054): the tests prove the requirement's text beyond its first four criteria, the rotation on a schedule.

title: Vulnerability and dependency management
requirement: Every pipeline shall run dependency scanning, static analysis, container scanning and produce a software bill of materials; builds shall fail on critical or high findings without an approved exception; exceptions shall expire; a monthly report shall list open findings per severity.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency with a critical vulnerability, When the pipeline runs, Then it fails naming the package. (error case)|Given an approved exception, When it expires, Then the build fails again until renewed.|Given a release, When published, Then its bill of materials is attached.

title: Secure development lifecycle
requirement: Every change shall pass code review by a second developer, automated tests, security checks and a threat-model check for new modules or external interfaces; security requirements shall be part of the definition of done; a yearly independent penetration test shall be performed and findings tracked.
rationale: Process controls expected by customers and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Given a pull request without review, When merge is attempted, Then it is blocked.|Given a new external interface, When the design is reviewed, Then a threat model record exists before build.|Given a penetration test finding rated high, When open for more than 30 days, Then it is escalated. (edge)|Given a change that lowers test coverage below the threshold, When merged, Then the pipeline refuses it. (error case)

title: Anti-tampering of files and uploads
requirement: Uploaded files shall be scanned for malware before they are stored as available, checked for type by content (not extension), limited in size per tenant setting, stored outside the web root with random names, and served only through signed, expiring links.
rationale: Files are a common attack path.
acceptance_criteria: Given an infected test file, When uploaded, Then it is quarantined, the user informed and the event audited. (error case)|Given a file renamed from executable to image, When uploaded, Then it is refused by content check.|Given a download link, When used after expiry, Then it is refused.

title: Security monitoring and incident response
requirement: Authentication failures, lockouts, permission denials, impersonations, break-glass, mass exports and configuration changes shall feed security alerts with thresholds; an incident runbook shall define severities, roles, communication and post-incident review; tenant notification duties (72 hours for personal data breaches) shall be built into the runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Given 100 permission denials from one principal in 10 minutes, When evaluated, Then an alert is raised.|Given an incident declared, When the runbook is followed, Then a post-incident review record exists within 10 days.|Given a mass export (over 10,000 records), When performed, Then an alert and an audit event exist. (edge)|Given an alert rule misconfigured, When evaluated, Then the rule is reported as failing instead of silently skipped. (error case)

title: Database conventions and schemas per module
requirement: Each module shall own one PostgreSQL schema named after the module; tables shall use snake_case names, a surrogate primary key, a public identifier where users see it, created and updated audit columns (by, at), optimistic concurrency version, and soft-delete flags where deletion is allowed; cross-module foreign keys are forbidden (references by identifier only) so that a module can be extracted later.
acceptance_criteria: Given a table without the standard columns, When the schema check runs in the pipeline, Then it fails naming the table.|Given a foreign key from one module's schema to another's, When the check runs, Then it fails. (error case)|Given a module removed, When its schema is dropped in a test database, Then other schemas remain valid.
notes: Carried: the current product already uses schemas per module.

title: Tenant-scoped data access
requirement: Repositories shall receive the tenant connection from the tenant context; the database role used by the application shall have no rights on other tenants' databases; a developer shall not be able to construct a cross-tenant query by accident.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository used outside a tenant context, When called, Then it throws a clear error at the call site. (error case)|Given the application role, When it attempts to connect to another tenant's database, Then the database refuses.|Given a control-plane service, When it needs tenant data (for health), Then it uses the provisioning role with read-only rights and the access is audited.

title: Migrations
requirement: Schema changes shall be code-first migrations per module, forward-only and backward compatible for one application version (expand and contract), applied to every tenant database by the fleet migration orchestrator (TF-213) in parallel waves after rehearsal on a clone, with a per-tenant status view and a documented rollback plan for each migration.
rationale: Many databases need safe, repeatable migrations.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new application version, When deployed, Then the previous version still runs against the migrated schema during the rollout.|Given a migration fails on one tenant, When the batch runs, Then other tenants continue and the failure is reported with the tenant named. (error case)|Given the fleet view, When opened, Then each tenant shows its schema version.

title: Optimistic concurrency everywhere
requirement: Every update shall carry the record version; a stale update shall be refused with a conflict response that includes the current version; the UI shall show a reload-and-retry message.
rationale: Gap: only some entities protected in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given two users save the same record, When the second saves, Then a conflict response is returned and the first save stands. (error case)|Given the conflict, When the UI reloads, Then the latest values are shown.|Given an API client without version, When updating, Then the request is refused as invalid.

title: Transactions, locks and atomic checks
requirement: Each operation shall run in one transaction; checks that depend on other rows (quantities, budgets, counters, uniqueness beyond constraints) shall lock the rows they depend on in a fixed order before checking; the data layer shall provide a helper for ordered row locks and an advisory lock helper for per-tenant singletons.
rationale: Gap: read-then-write races in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given two concurrent operations consuming the last unit of a counter, When both run, Then exactly one succeeds.|Given an operation that locks rows out of order, When the lock order checker runs in tests, Then it fails.|Given a transaction fails after audit rows were written, When rolled back, Then no audit rows remain for the failed operation. (edge)|Given a lock wait that exceeds 10 seconds, When detected, Then the operation fails with a retryable error instead of hanging. (error case)

title: Transactional outbox
requirement: Domain events shall be written to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business change; the worker shall deliver them at least once in order per aggregate, mark them delivered, and retry with backoff; consumers shall be idempotent by event identifier.
acceptance_criteria: Given a business change committed, When the worker runs, Then the event is dispatched within 10 seconds.|Given a consumer failure, When retried, Then the event is delivered again until the retry limit, then parked in a dead-letter list with a reason. (error case)|Given the same event delivered twice, When consumed, Then the consumer produces no duplicate effect.

title: Bulk loading
requirement: Imports and migrations shall load large data sets with the database's native bulk copy, in batches, with validation before load and a per-row error report.
rationale: Performance and the IronSaaS rule for bulk data.
acceptance_criteria: Given 100,000 rows, When imported, Then the load completes within 5 minutes and uses bulk copy.|Given 10 invalid rows, When imported, Then valid rows load and the 10 are reported with reasons. (error case)|Given a load interrupted, When restarted, Then already loaded batches are not duplicated.

title: Backups and point-in-time recovery
requirement: Backups shall run once per database server (continuous archiving of the whole server plus a daily base backup, retained 35 days, encrypted, in the deployment's region) so that effort does not grow with the number of tenants, while restore shall be possible per tenant database to any point in time within the retention without affecting other tenants (TF-214); object storage shall be versioned; a quarterly restore drill per environment shall be recorded.
rationale: Database per tenant makes per-tenant restore possible.
acceptance_criteria: Given a restore request to a point in time, When performed in the drill, Then the tenant is usable within 2 hours.|Given backups missing for a day, When checked, Then an alert is raised and the fleet view shows it. (error case)|Given a restore of tenant A, When done, Then tenant B is unaffected.

title: Reference data and seeding
requirement: System reference data (lookups, permissions, roles, settings defaults, templates) shall be versioned in code and applied by idempotent seed steps during provisioning and upgrades; tenant-maintained data shall never be overwritten by seeds.
acceptance_criteria: Given a seed run twice, When finished, Then no duplicates exist.|Given a tenant changed a seeded value flagged as tenant-editable, When a new seed version runs, Then the tenant value is kept.|Given a seed step fails, When run, Then the upgrade stops for that tenant and reports. (error case)
notes: Carried: 106 lookup groups and 84 settings in the current product.

title: Data export and portability
requirement: A tenant administrator shall be able to request a full export of the tenant's data (business records as CSV or JSON per entity, files, audit) delivered as an encrypted archive with a manifest; exports shall be audited and rate limited.
rationale: Customer trust, contract exit, backup for the customer.
acceptance_criteria: Given an export request, When completed, Then the archive contains every entity with a manifest listing counts.|Given a second request within the limit window, When made, Then it is refused with the next allowed time. (error case)|Given the archive, When opened with the provided key, Then files and data are readable.

title: Generic approval workflow engine
requirement: Workflow shall provide, for any record type registered by a module: approval configurations with conditions on registered fields (operators per data type, dynamic dates), chain types (specific approvers, submission blocking, submission warning, exception handling), fixed ordered stages (default 3, configurable per record type) with names, priority, approvers and observers (users, groups, dynamic resolvers), parallel or sequential completion per stage, skip rules, frozen chain instances on submission, and the actions approve, reject (comment required per setting), cancel, add approver, remove approver, bypass (permission), reassign.
rationale: Carried from the current product's engine; made generic and complete.
acceptance_criteria: Given configurations for stages 1 and 3, When a record is submitted, Then stage 2 is created as Skipped and stage 1 is In Progress.|Given a blocking configuration matches, When submitted, Then submission is refused with the configured message and no chain is created. (error case)|Given parallel completion requires all approvers, When one approves, Then the stage stays In Progress until all have approved.
notes: Includes dynamic resolvers registered by modules (budget owner, manager chain, authority matrix).

title: Dynamic approver resolvers
requirement: Modules shall register dynamic resolvers (for example line manager up to N levels, owner of a referenced record, members of a group linked to a record attribute, authority matrix by amount band and dimensions); the engine shall resolve them at submission, record the resolved identities on the chain, and apply a configured fallback (skip stage, assign fallback user, or refuse submission) when a resolver returns nobody.
rationale: Carried; adds explicit fallback behaviour (an open question in the current product).
