acceptance_criteria: Given a resolver returning two users, When the chain is built, Then both are approvers of the stage.|Given a resolver returning nobody and fallback "refuse", When submitted, Then submission is refused naming the resolver. (error case)|Given fallback "skip", When nobody resolves, Then the stage is Skipped with an audit note.

title: Workflow SLA, reminders and escalation
requirement: Each stage shall have a configurable target time; the engine shall send reminders at configured intervals, escalate to a configured principal (manager or group) after the target, and show age and overdue flags in queues and dashboards.
rationale: Gap: setting existed without a job in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stage target of 2 days, When 2 days pass without decision, Then the escalation principal is notified and the item is flagged overdue.|Given reminders every 24 hours, When 48 hours pass, Then two reminders were sent to pending approvers.|Given the decision is made before the target, When evaluated, Then no reminder or escalation is sent. (edge)|Given an escalation principal that no longer exists, When escalation runs, Then the tenant administrators are notified and the item flagged. (error case)

title: Workflow queue and history
requirement: Every principal shall have one queue of items pending their action across all record types (as approver, delegate or observer) with stage labels, record summary, age and direct actions; every record shall show its current chain and the full history of all chains with decisions, comments and signatures.
acceptance_criteria: Given items pending in three record types, When the queue loads, Then all appear with type, identifier, requester, amount, stage and age.|Given an item actioned, When done, Then it leaves the queue without reload.|Given a user without the history permission, When opening history, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: State machine framework
requirement: Modules shall declare the states and allowed transitions of their records (with guards, required permission, side effects) in one place; the framework shall enforce transitions, record every transition in audit with reason, and expose the allowed actions for the current user and record so the UI shows only valid buttons.
rationale: Status logic was scattered in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transition not allowed from the current state, When requested, Then it is refused with the current and requested state named. (error case)|Given a record, When the UI asks for allowed actions, Then only transitions whose guards and permissions pass are returned.|Given a transition, When committed, Then an audit event with before and after state exists.

title: Workflow configuration management
requirement: Approval configurations shall be versioned; in-flight chains keep the version they were built with; configurations can be simulated against an existing record to show the chain that would be built; import and export between tenants shall be supported.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configuration changed, When an in-flight record is viewed, Then its chain is unchanged.|Given a simulation on a record, When run, Then the stages and approvers that would result are shown without creating a chain.|Given an import with unknown fields, When run, Then it is refused with the fields listed. (error case)

title: Workflow notifications
requirement: The engine shall emit standard events (action required, peer rejected, revoked, submitted for observers, final status to requester, escalated, reminder) that notifications deliver through templates; products add no notification code for approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stage becomes In Progress, When processed, Then each approver gets an action-required notification through their channels.|Given the final decision, When made, Then the requester is notified.|Given notifications blocked by the kill switch, When processed, Then the events are still recorded and delivered later. (edge)|Given a template missing for a workflow key, When the event fires, Then the delivery is marked Failed and alerted, and the approval still proceeds. (error case)

title: Tasks and queries between parties
requirement: Workflow shall provide generic tasks (type, priority, title, description, assignee principal or external party, linked record, attachments) with states Draft, Open, Reopened, Resolved, Closed, reassignment and notifications, usable by any module including supplier portals.
rationale: Carried from tasks, queries and issues.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task assigned to an external party user, When created, Then they see it in their portal queue and are notified.|Given a Closed task, When resolve is attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a reopen, When done, Then the assignee is notified and the history shows both events.

title: Comments and conversations
requirement: Any record shall support comments (author, time, text, mentions, attachments) with edit and soft delete by the author, visibility rules (internal only or shared with external parties), and mention notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Given an internal-only comment, When a supplier user views the record, Then the comment is hidden.|Given a mention, When saved, Then the mentioned user is notified.|Given another user edits a comment, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Business calendar and working time
requirement: Tenants shall define working days, holidays and hours per organisation unit; SLA timers shall count working time when configured.
acceptance_criteria: Given a target of 2 working days and a weekend, When computed, Then the deadline skips the weekend.|Given a holiday added, When timers are recomputed, Then deadlines move.|Given no calendar configured, When computed, Then calendar days are used. (edge)|Given a calendar with an invalid time range, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: A kernel requirement, confirmed by the PRD split. The business layer's approval configurations (BF-141) count their stage targets in its working time, per unit, and so will the due dates of tasks.

title: REST API conventions
requirement: All operations shall be REST resources with plural nouns, standard verbs, consistent naming (snake_case JSON), a standard response envelope for lists (data, meta, links) and problem details for errors (type, title, status, detail, error code, correlation id, field errors), documented in OpenAPI generated from code.
rationale: Carried from the partner interface contract; now for every surface.
acceptance_criteria: Given any error, When returned, Then it follows the problem format with a stable error code.|Given a list, When returned, Then it carries total count, page information and navigation links.|Given the OpenAPI document, When validated, Then every operation has permission, request and response schemas documented. (edge)|Given a request body that does not match the schema, When received, Then a problem response names the fields and nothing is processed. (error case)

title: Paging, filtering, sorting and sparse fields
requirement: List operations shall support cursor or offset paging (max page size 200), filtering with a bounded grammar (field, operator, value; operators per type), multi-field sorting and sparse field selection, implemented once in the data layer and whitelisted per resource.
rationale: One grammar for UI grids and partners.
acceptance_criteria: Given a filter on a non-whitelisted field, When requested, Then a validation problem names the field. (error case)|Given a page size of 500, When requested, Then it is capped at 200 and the cap is returned in meta.|Given a sort by two fields, When requested, Then results are ordered accordingly.

title: API versioning and deprecation
requirement: The API shall be versioned in the path (v1, v2); a version shall be supported for at least 12 months after its successor; deprecations shall be announced through response headers, documentation and tenant notifications; breaking changes only in a new version.
acceptance_criteria: Given v1 and v2 both deployed, When v1 is called, Then it still works with its original contract.|Given a deprecated version, When called, Then the response carries a deprecation header with the sunset date.|Given a breaking change proposed within a version, When reviewed, Then the contract test fails. (error case)

title: Idempotent writes
requirement: Create and action operations shall accept an idempotency key header; the same key with the same body within 24 hours shall return the original result without repeating the effect; the same key with a different body shall be refused.
rationale: Safe retries for clients and partners.
acceptance_criteria: Given a create sent twice with the same key, When processed, Then one record exists and both responses are identical.|Given the same key with a different body, When sent, Then a conflict problem is returned. (error case)|Given the key expires after 24 hours, When reused, Then a new record is created.

title: Conditional requests and caching
requirement: Read operations shall return ETags; updates may send If-Match to avoid lost updates; list and reference-data reads shall support If-None-Match to save bandwidth.
acceptance_criteria: Given an If-Match with a stale ETag, When updating, Then a precondition-failed problem is returned. (error case)|Given If-None-Match with the current ETag, When reading, Then not-modified is returned.|Given no headers, When reading, Then the full response is returned with an ETag.

title: Webhooks
requirement: Tenant administrators and partners shall subscribe URLs to event types with a shared secret; deliveries shall be signed (HMAC with timestamp), retried with exponential backoff for 24 hours, logged with status and response, replayable from the console, and paused automatically after persistent failure with a notification.
acceptance_criteria: Given an event, When delivered, Then the payload is signed and the receiver can verify it.|Given the receiver returns errors for 24 hours, When exhausted, Then the subscription is paused and the owner notified. (error case)|Given a replay request, When made, Then the event is re-sent with a replay marker.

title: Long-running operations
requirement: Operations that take longer than a few seconds (exports, imports, mass updates) shall return an operation resource with status, progress, result link and cancel action, and shall notify the requester on completion.
acceptance_criteria: Given an export started, When polled, Then progress increases and the result link appears at completion.|Given a cancel, When requested while running, Then the operation stops and status is Cancelled.|Given a failed operation, When polled, Then status is Failed with a reason. (error case)

title: Partner API gateway behaviour
requirement: Partner traffic (service accounts, API keys) shall pass through the same API with per-principal rate limits, quotas, request and response logging (without personal data), usage metering and an optional allow-list of resources per service account.
rationale: Carried from the partner interface; now the same API, not a second one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a service account limited to two resources, When it calls a third, Then it is forbidden. (error case)|Given partner calls, When metered, Then counts appear in usage.|Given a partner request, When logged, Then personal data in bodies is masked.

title: SDKs and documentation portal
requirement: Client libraries for TypeScript and Python shall be generated from the OpenAPI document on each release, and a documentation portal shall publish the API reference, guides, changelog and a sandbox tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release, When published, Then SDKs with the same version number exist.|Given a breaking change in a new version, When the portal updates, Then the changelog lists it.|Given the sandbox tenant, When a partner registers, Then they can call the API with test data. (edge)|Given SDK generation fails on an invalid OpenAPI document, When the release runs, Then it is blocked. (error case)

title: Bulk and batch operations
requirement: The API shall offer batch create and update for selected resources (up to 1,000 items per call) with per-item results, and bulk export operations that stream results.
acceptance_criteria: Given a batch of 1,000 items with 3 invalid, When processed, Then 997 succeed and 3 are reported with reasons.|Given a batch of 1,001 items, When sent, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a streamed export, When consumed, Then memory on the server stays bounded.

title: Domain event catalogue
requirement: Modules shall declare their domain events (name, version, payload schema, description) in a catalogue exposed to administrators and partners; payloads shall carry tenant, record identifiers, actor, time and a schema version; personal data shall be limited to identifiers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new event, When declared, Then it appears in the catalogue with its schema.|Given a payload that fails its schema, When emitted, Then emission fails in tests. (error case)|Given an event version change, When published, Then both versions are listed with the deprecation date.

title: Event subscriptions inside the platform
requirement: Modules shall subscribe to events of other modules through the event dispatcher (in-process, from the outbox), never by direct calls into another module's internals; handlers shall be idempotent and may fail independently.
acceptance_criteria: Given a handler fails, When others run, Then they complete and only the failed one retries.|Given a handler processes the same event twice, When run, Then no duplicate effect occurs.|Given a module calls another module's repository directly, When the build check runs, Then it fails. (error case)

title: Event replay and inspection
requirement: Administrators shall inspect delivered and failed events per tenant, replay a failed event to a handler or webhook, and see the dead-letter list with reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dead-lettered event, When replayed, Then the handler runs again and the status updates.|Given an event older than the retention, When searched, Then it is reported as archived.|Given a user without the events permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Message broker readiness
requirement: The dispatcher shall be replaceable by a broker-based implementation (open source) without changes to publishers or handlers, when a measured need appears (cross-process consumers, very high volume).
rationale: Avoid designing it out while keeping version 1 simple.
acceptance_criteria: Given the broker implementation enabled in a test environment, When events flow, Then handlers receive them unchanged.|Given the broker down, When publishing, Then events stay in the outbox and are delivered on recovery.|Given no broker configured, When starting, Then the in-process dispatcher is used. (edge)|Given a broker publish failure, When detected, Then the outbox keeps the event and the failure is alerted. (error case)

title: Outbound integration connectors
requirement: Integration shall provide a connector pattern (configuration, mapping, schedule or event trigger, retry, error queue, run history) for pushing records to external systems (ERP, finance, HR) with the first connectors defined by products.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connector configured with a mapping, When an event fires, Then the mapped payload is sent and the run recorded.|Given the target rejects a payload, When retried per policy, Then it lands in the error queue with the response. (error case)|Given a mapping changed, When the next run happens, Then the new mapping applies.

title: Background jobs
requirement: Jobs shall be defined in code with name, schedule or trigger, tenant scope (all tenants or one), timeout, retry policy and concurrency rule; the worker shall run them in clustered mode so that one job instance runs at a time per tenant unless parallel is allowed; jobs shall be idempotent.
rationale: Carried: 9 scheduled jobs; now with a framework.
acceptance_criteria: Given a job scheduled every minute, When two worker nodes run, Then exactly one executes per tenant per interval.|Given a job exceeds its timeout, When detected, Then it is cancelled, logged and retried per policy. (error case)|Given a job runs twice due to a retry, When finished, Then the effect is the same as one run.

title: Job console
requirement: Administrators and operators shall see jobs, schedules, last and next runs, durations, failures with messages, backlog per tenant, and shall be able to pause, resume, trigger and re-run a job; all actions audited.
acceptance_criteria: Given a failed job, When viewed, Then the error and the run log are shown.|Given pause, When applied, Then the job skips runs until resumed and the state is visible.|Given a user without the jobs permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Per-tenant fairness and priority
requirement: Because workers are per tenant, fairness shall be enforced at the shared resources: each tenant unit has connection limits on the database server, CPU and memory quotas on its containers, and rate limits on shared services, so that one tenant's backlog cannot starve others; inside a unit, priority classes (interactive, normal, bulk) order the work.
acceptance_criteria: Given tenant A queues 10,000 exports and saturates its own quota, When tenant B queues one, Then B's export starts within one minute because A cannot exceed its connection and CPU limits.|Given an interactive-class item, When queued, Then it runs before bulk items.|Given a tenant suspended, When its jobs are due, Then they are skipped and logged. (edge)|Given a priority class not defined, When work is queued, Then it is refused in tests. (error case)

title: Retries, dead letters and alerts
requirement: Failed work shall retry with exponential backoff and jitter up to a policy limit, then move to a dead-letter list with the error; alerts shall fire on dead-letter growth and on jobs not run on schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transient failure, When retried, Then the delay grows per policy.|Given the limit reached, When exhausted, Then the item is dead-lettered and an alert raised. (error case)|Given a job missed its schedule by more than one interval, When evaluated, Then an alert is raised.

title: Maintenance jobs supplied by Foundation
requirement: Foundation shall ship jobs for: session cleanup, token cleanup, outbox delivery, notification delivery, webhook delivery, retention and archival, audit chain verification, metering, file quarantine purge, orphan file purge, backup verification, flag and setting cache refresh.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new tenant, When provisioned, Then all maintenance jobs are active for it.|Given the orphan file purge, When run, Then files unreferenced for 30 days are removed and audited.|Given backup verification fails, When run, Then an alert is raised. (error case)

title: Distributed tracing and correlation
requirement: Every request, job and event shall carry a correlation id and produce an OpenTelemetry trace with tenant, principal (identifier only), operation and outcome attributes; the correlation id shall be returned to clients and shown on error pages so users can quote it to support.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request, When traced, Then spans exist for the API, the database calls and any outbound calls, all under one trace id.|Given an error page, When shown, Then the correlation id is visible.|Given a job triggered by a request, When traced, Then it links to the originating trace. (edge)|Given the trace exporter unavailable, When requests run, Then they still complete and spans are buffered then dropped with a metric counting the loss. (error case)

title: Metrics and SLIs
requirement: The platform shall export metrics per tenant and operation: request rate, error rate, latency distribution, saturation (connections, queue depth, worker utilisation), job outcomes, notification outcomes, and shall define SLIs for availability and latency per surface with SLOs and error budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant, When the dashboard loads, Then its request rate, error rate and latency percentiles are shown.|Given an SLO burn rate above threshold, When evaluated, Then an alert fires within 5 minutes.|Given metrics export fails, When detected, Then an alert is raised through a second channel. (error case)

title: Structured logs with scrubbing
requirement: Logs shall be structured JSON with level, time, correlation id, tenant, module, message and properties, exported through OpenTelemetry; a scrubber shall mask personal data patterns (emails, phones, identifiers) and secret patterns before export; log level shall be adjustable per module at runtime.
rationale: Useful logs that are safe to store.
acceptance_criteria: Given a log with an email in a property, When exported, Then the email is masked.|Given a module set to debug at runtime, When requests run, Then debug lines appear within one minute without restart.|Given a secret pattern in a message, When exported, Then it is masked. (error case)

title: Health checks
requirement: Each host shall expose liveness and readiness checks (database, secrets store, object storage, telemetry exporter, job scheduler), and the control plane shall expose per-tenant health used by the fleet view and a public status page.
acceptance_criteria: Given the database unreachable, When readiness is checked, Then it fails and the node is removed from rotation.|Given all dependencies healthy, When checked, Then readiness passes within 1 second.|Given a tenant database down, When fleet health runs, Then only that tenant is flagged. (edge)|Given a readiness check that times out, When evaluated, Then it is reported as failed, not as passed. (error case)

title: Dashboards and alerting
requirement: Foundation shall ship dashboards (platform overview, per tenant, per module, jobs, notifications, security) and alert rules (SLO burn, error spikes, job failures, dead letters, backup failures, certificate expiry, disk and connection saturation, security thresholds) with routing to on-call channels and runbook links.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh environment, When telemetry is deployed, Then the dashboards exist and show data within 10 minutes.|Given a certificate expiring in 14 days, When evaluated, Then an alert fires.|Given an alert, When opened, Then it links to the runbook. (edge)|Given an alert routed to a channel that fails, When sent, Then it falls back to the secondary channel. (error case)

title: Client-side telemetry
requirement: The UI shell shall report page load timing, API call outcomes, unhandled errors and user-visible errors with correlation ids, respecting a tenant privacy setting that can disable it.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unhandled UI error, When it occurs, Then an event with stack and correlation id is exported.|Given client telemetry disabled by the tenant, When the UI runs, Then nothing is exported.|Given a slow page (over 3 seconds), When measured, Then it appears in the UI performance dashboard. (edge)|Given a client event over the allowed size, When sent, Then it is rejected and counted. (error case)

title: Usage analytics for product teams
requirement: The platform shall record feature usage events (screen opened, action performed) per tenant with identifiers only, exportable to the product analytics tool chosen by the team.
acceptance_criteria: Given a screen opened, When recorded, Then tenant, user identifier, screen and time are stored.|Given personal data in an event property, When scrubbed, Then it is masked.|Given a tenant opts out, When recorded, Then events are dropped. (edge)|Given an event with a disallowed property name, When recorded, Then it is rejected in tests. (error case)

title: Externalised UI strings and translation workflow
requirement: All UI text shall come from resource files keyed per module; the build shall fail on hard-coded user-facing strings in components; translations shall be editable by translators in a file format they can use (JSON or XLIFF), with missing-translation reports and a fallback to English.
acceptance_criteria: Given a component with a literal string, When the lint check runs, Then it fails.|Given a missing key in Spanish, When rendered, Then English is shown and the key is listed in the report.|Given a new language file added, When loaded, Then the language is selectable without a release.|Given a translation file with invalid syntax, When loaded, Then the build fails naming the file. (error case)

title: Server messages and errors localised
requirement: Validation and business messages returned by the API shall be message codes with parameters; the UI (or API client) shall render them in the user's language; the catalogue of codes shall be documented.
rationale: One message, many languages, stable codes for partners.
acceptance_criteria: Given a validation failure, When returned, Then the response has a code and parameters and the UI shows the translated text.|Given an unknown code, When rendered, Then a generic translated message with the code is shown. (error case)|Given a partner client, When it receives a code, Then it can look it up in the documented catalogue.
notes: Gap: current messages are English literals in code with typos.

title: Locale formats
requirement: Dates, times, numbers and currencies shall follow the user's locale with tenant overrides (including Indian digit grouping), timezones shall be per user with tenant default, and the UI shall show the timezone next to times where it matters (deadlines, auctions).
acceptance_criteria: Given the Indian grouping format, When an amount renders, Then it shows 12,34,567.89.|Given a user in another zone, When a deadline renders, Then it is converted and the zone named.|Given an invalid format string in a tenant override, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Multi-language master data
requirement: Modules shall be able to mark text attributes of master data as translatable (name, description); the data layer shall store translations per language with a default, and reads shall return the user's language with fallback.
rationale: Multinational tenants. Decided: later, together with AI-assisted translation; version 1 stores data as Unicode in any language (TF-145).
acceptance_criteria: Given a category with English and Spanish names, When a Spanish user lists categories, Then Spanish names appear.|Given no Spanish translation, When listed, Then the default language value appears.|Given a translation edited, When saved, Then it is audited like any field. (edge)|Given a translation for a language not enabled for the tenant, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Right-to-left and script readiness
requirement: The shell shall support right-to-left layout and non-Latin scripts without layout breakage.
acceptance_criteria: Given an RTL language selected, When pages render, Then layout mirrors correctly.|Given long non-Latin strings, When rendered, Then no truncation hides meaning.|Given mixed-direction text in a field, When rendered, Then it is readable. (edge)|Given a component that breaks in RTL, When the visual test runs, Then it fails. (error case)

title: Unicode and locale-aware text handling
requirement: All text fields shall store Unicode without length loss for any script, normalise text for comparison (uniqueness, search) with a documented normalisation form, sort lists by the user's locale collation where the database supports it, and support search across scripts; no field shall assume Latin characters.
rationale: Decided: data is in any language from day one; translation comes later.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier name in Hindi and another in Arabic, When saved and listed, Then both display correctly and sort by the user's locale.|Given two names differing only by Unicode normalisation form, When the uniqueness check runs, Then they are treated as the same.|Given a field with a byte-based length limit, When reviewed by the schema check, Then it fails; limits are in characters. (error case)

title: Notification templates and channels
requirement: Modules shall declare notification keys (audience, description, available placeholders); tenants shall edit templates per key and language (subject, body in rich text, placeholders validated); channels shall include email, in-app and SMS in version 1 with webhooks and push later; rendering shall fail safely when a placeholder cannot be resolved.
rationale: Carried 41 keys; adds languages and validation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template with an unknown placeholder, When saved, Then it is refused naming the placeholder. (error case)|Given a user whose language is Spanish, When notified, Then the Spanish template is used if present, else the default.|Given rendering fails, When processed, Then the delivery is marked Failed and the failure alerted, never sent half-filled.

title: Preferences, mandates and digests
requirement: Users shall set channel preferences per key; administrators shall set defaults and mandates (channel forced on); users may choose digests (hourly or daily summary) for non-urgent keys; keys marked urgent ignore digests.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mandate for a key, When the user tries to turn its channel off, Then the change is refused with the mandate shown. (error case)|Given daily digest chosen, When five non-urgent notifications occur, Then one summary email is sent at the configured time.|Given an urgent key, When digests are chosen, Then it is still sent immediately.

title: Delivery tracking and resend
requirement: Every notification shall record per channel: queued, sent, failed with reason, blocked, read (in-app); administrators shall search deliveries and resend; bounces and complaints from the email provider shall be recorded and suppress further email to invalid addresses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a hard bounce, When received, Then the address is suppressed and the user and administrator informed.|Given a failed delivery, When resent, Then a new attempt is recorded.|Given a search by user and period, When run, Then all deliveries with status appear. (edge)|Given a resend by a user without the permission, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: In-app notification centre and real-time push
requirement: The shell shall show an in-app notification centre with unread count updated in real time, mark as read, open the linked record, and archive; the real-time channel shall be reused by products for live updates.
rationale: Carried; one real-time channel for the platform.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new notification, When the user is connected, Then the count updates without reload within 2 seconds.|Given a notification opened, When read, Then the status is Read across devices.|Given the connection drops, When restored, Then the centre reloads the current state. (edge)|Given a notification opened by a user who is not its recipient, When requested by identifier, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Email sending infrastructure
requirement: Email shall be sent through configurable SMTP or provider adapters per tenant or per platform, with DKIM and SPF guidance, per-tenant sender identity, rate control, retry and bounce handling, and a test-send action in the console.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant sender configured, When a test send is made, Then the email arrives with the tenant's sender name.|Given the provider rejects, When retried per policy, Then the failure is recorded with the provider message. (error case)|Given the platform sender, When a tenant has none, Then it is used with the tenant name in the display name.

title: SMS and other channels
requirement: SMS shall be sent through a provider adapter per region with cost controls and opt-out handling; push notifications and chat connectors (for example team chat webhooks) shall be addable as channels through the same adapter interface.
acceptance_criteria: Given an SMS over the tenant's daily cap, When queued, Then it is held and the administrator informed. (error case)|Given an opted-out number, When queued, Then it is not sent.|Given a chat connector channel added, When a key is routed to it, Then messages arrive in the chat tool.

title: Announcements
requirement: Administrators shall publish announcements (title, body, audience by unit or role, start and end dates, severity) shown in the shell banner and the notification centre until dismissed; operators shall publish platform-wide maintenance notices to all tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Given an announcement for unit A, When a user of unit B logs in, Then it is not shown.|Given a maintenance notice, When published by an operator, Then all tenants see it with the scheduled time.|Given an announcement dismissed, When the user logs in again, Then it is not shown. (edge)|Given an announcement with an end date before the start date, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: File storage service
requirement: Files shall be stored in object storage under tenant prefixes with random keys, with metadata (name, type, size, hash, uploader, record link, classification), versions, soft delete and retention; access shall be through signed, expiring links generated after a permission check on the linked record.
acceptance_criteria: Given an upload, When stored, Then its hash is recorded and a later download verifies it.|Given a download request for a file on a record the user may not read, When made, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a file replaced, When viewed, Then the version history is available.

title: Upload rules
requirement: Allowed types (by content), size limits, per-record count limits and required attachment types shall be configurable per tenant and per record type; uploads shall be scanned (TF-078) and shown as available only after the scan passes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a type outside the allowed list, When uploaded, Then it is refused with the allowed types.|Given a required attachment type missing, When the record is submitted, Then submission is refused naming the type. (error case)|Given a file scanning, When viewed, Then it shows as pending until the scan passes.

title: Document rendering
requirement: Foundation shall render documents (orders, receipts, letters) from HTML templates with placeholders and tenant branding into PDF, store the rendered file on the record with the template version, and allow preview before issue.
rationale: Carried PO and GRN templates; made generic.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template and a record, When rendered, Then a PDF is produced with the tenant logo and stored with the template version.|Given a placeholder unresolved, When rendered, Then rendering fails with the placeholder named. (error case)|Given the template changed later, When the old document is viewed, Then the original PDF is shown.

title: Document templates management
requirement: Tenant administrators shall maintain templates per document type, organisation unit and language, with versioning, preview against sample data and validation of placeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template for unit A, When a record of A is rendered, Then that template is used.|Given no template for the unit, When rendered, Then the tenant default is used.|Given a template with invalid markup, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Signature capture and signed documents
requirement: The platform shall capture drawn or typed signatures and acceptance clicks, bind them to a document version hash and the signer's identity (TF-063), and produce a signed PDF with a signature page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a signature captured, When stored, Then the document hash and identity are linked.|Given the document changes, When viewed, Then the signature shows the earlier version.|Given signing by an unauthenticated session, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: File retention, archival and purge
requirement: Files shall follow the retention policy of their record; deleted files shall be kept for 30 days then purged; unreferenced files shall be purged after 30 days; archived files shall move to cheaper storage classes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a deleted file, When 30 days pass, Then it is purged and audited.|Given a file under legal hold, When purge runs, Then it is skipped. (edge)|Given a purge job failure, When detected, Then an alert is raised. (error case)

title: Document numbering service
requirement: Foundation shall provide numbering sequences per record type and optional dimension (organisation unit, year) with prefix, suffix, length, leading zeros, reset rules, and atomic allocation that never reuses a number; numbers are allocated at submission for documents and at creation for master records.
acceptance_criteria: Given two documents numbered at once, When allocated, Then they receive different numbers.|Given a reset per year, When the year changes, Then the counter restarts and the year appears in the number.|Given a sequence set inactive, When allocation is requested, Then it is refused with a configuration message. (error case)
notes: A kernel requirement, confirmed by the PRD split. The business layer's number series (BF-163) configure it per document type and unit, with a legal entity's numbering initials as a dynamic prefix (BF-001).

title: Application shell
requirement: The shell shall provide login flows, navigation built from module manifests filtered by entitlement, permission and flags, a header (search, notifications, help, profile), page layout patterns (list, record with tabs, wizard), global error handling with correlation ids, session expiry handling, and a product registration API so product UIs plug in without touching shell code.
acceptance_criteria: Given a module without entitlement, When the shell renders, Then its navigation is absent.|Given an unhandled error, When it occurs, Then a friendly page shows the correlation id and the shell stays usable.|Given a product registers a route, When loaded, Then it appears under its module in navigation with its permission guard. (edge)|Given a product route registered without a permission guard, When the shell starts, Then it fails in development and the route is hidden in production. (error case)

title: Design system
requirement: A component library on Mantine shall provide forms (schema-driven, inline validation, server error mapping), one data grid component wrapping AG Grid (Community first; Enterprise features such as pivoting, grouping, Excel-like editing and Excel export switched on by licence without product changes) with server paging, filtering, sorting, column chooser, saved views, export and keyboard navigation, record header with status and actions, approval panel, attachment panel, history panel, comment panel, dialogs, empty and loading states, and theming tokens; products shall use these components only.
rationale: Consistency and speed; replaces the commercial grid.
acceptance_criteria: Given a product screen using a raw third-party grid, When the lint check runs, Then it fails.|Given a grid with saved view, When the user returns, Then the view is restored.|Given a form with a server validation error, When returned, Then the error appears on the field. (edge)|Given a grid request for a page size over the limit, When made, Then it is capped and a notice shown. (error case)

title: Accessibility
requirement: All shell and library components shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA (contrast, labels, focus order, keyboard operation, screen-reader names, reduced motion); automated checks shall run on every build and a manual audit each quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Given the automated scan, When run on the component gallery, Then zero AA violations are reported.|Given a grid, When operated by keyboard only, Then rows can be selected and actions triggered.|Given a colour-only status indicator, When reviewed, Then it also has text or icon. (edge)|Given a pull request that introduces an accessibility violation, When the pipeline runs, Then it fails. (error case)

title: Theming and white label
requirement: Tenants shall set logo, colours (within contrast rules), favicon, product name shown in the shell and email templates, login page text and footer links; the platform shall validate contrast and preview before applying.
acceptance_criteria: Given a colour pair below contrast ratio 4.5:1, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a logo uploaded, When the shell loads, Then it appears in header, login and emails.|Given no branding set, When loaded, Then the platform default applies.

title: Responsive and offline-tolerant behaviour
requirement: The shell shall work on desktop and tablet widths, show clear offline and reconnecting states, keep unsaved form data on connection loss for the session, and avoid duplicate submissions on retry (idempotency keys).
acceptance_criteria: Given the network drops during a form, When restored, Then the typed data is still present.|Given a submit retried after a timeout, When processed, Then one record exists.|Given a tablet width, When pages render, Then no horizontal scrolling of the page body occurs. (edge)|Given a form submitted twice within the idempotency window, When processed, Then the second returns the first result and no duplicate is created. (error case)

title: Help and guidance
requirement: The shell shall support contextual help per screen (tenant-editable text and links), guided tours for first use, and a support page with the correlation id of the last error.
acceptance_criteria: Given help text for a screen, When the help icon is clicked, Then it is shown.|Given first login, When the home page loads, Then the tour offers to start and can be dismissed permanently.|Given no help configured, When clicked, Then a default page is shown. (edge)|Given help text with a script tag, When saved, Then it is sanitised. (error case)

title: Operator console
requirement: Operators shall have a console for tenants (create, lifecycle, entitlements, plans, limits, flags, hostnames, regions), fleet health, jobs across tenants, releases and migrations status, security alerts, break-glass, platform notices, usage and billing; every action audited and permission-controlled with operator roles.
acceptance_criteria: Given an operator without the entitlement permission, When changing entitlements, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a tenant created in the console, When provisioning completes, Then the console shows Active and the administrator invitation sent.|Given the fleet view, When a tenant is unhealthy, Then it is highlighted with the failing check.

title: Operator roles and dual control
requirement: Operator access shall use the same identity and authorization modules with MFA mandatory, roles (read-only operator, support operator, platform administrator, security officer), and dual control for destructive or sensitive actions (decommission, break-glass, entitlement removal, retention changes).
rationale: The control plane is the crown jewel.
acceptance_criteria: Given an operator without MFA, When logging in, Then enrolment is forced before access.|Given a decommission started, When the same operator tries to approve, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a read-only operator, When viewing tenants, Then no action buttons are shown and the API refuses writes.

title: Tenant administration console
requirement: Tenant administrators shall have a console for users and invitations, roles and assignments, organisation units, SSO and SCIM, MFA policy, sessions, settings, notification templates and preferences defaults, document templates, numbering, custom fields and lookups, webhooks, service accounts and API keys, jobs status, audit search, data export and privacy requests; grouped by area with search.
acceptance_criteria: Given an administrator, When the console opens, Then only areas they have permission for are shown.|Given an SSO configuration saved, When tested with the test action, Then the result is shown before enabling.|Given an action, When performed, Then it is audited. (edge)|Given an administrator saves an SSO configuration that fails the test, When they try to enable it, Then enabling is refused until the test passes. (error case)

title: Self-service tenant sign-up
requirement: The platform may offer self-service sign-up that creates a trial tenant after email verification and operator-defined guardrails (limits, regions, plan).
acceptance_criteria: Given a verified email, When sign-up completes, Then a trial tenant is provisioned within 15 minutes.|Given a disposable email domain, When used, Then sign-up is refused. (error case)|Given the daily sign-up cap reached, When another arrives, Then it is queued with a message.

title: Repository, conventions and scaffolding
requirement: One repository shall hold Foundation and products with the layout in section 3.5, enforced conventions (naming, module boundaries, standard columns, owning organisation, permission declarations, tracked entities, externalised strings) as build checks, a scaffolding tool that creates a new module or a new entity with endpoint, service, repository, migration, permissions, tests and UI screens from templates, and a complete local stack (control plane, fleet orchestrator in single-node mode, tenant units, Supplier Network, database, object storage, secrets and telemetry) that starts on a developer laptop with one command and provisions a tenant with a second command.
rationale: Simplicity and speed for new developers (P1).
acceptance_criteria: Given the scaffolding tool run for a new entity, When finished, Then the application builds, the entity has list and detail screens, and tests pass.|Given a module boundary violated, When the build runs, Then it fails naming the files. (error case)|Given a new developer following the README on a 32 GB laptop, When they start, Then the full local stack runs and a tenant is provisioned within one hour, with a slim profile available without the telemetry stack.|Given the repository, When the architecture tests run, Then the folders of section 3.5 are at its root: the source, the tests, the tools, the platform's infrastructure, the shell and the documents.

title: Continuous integration and delivery
requirement: Every change shall build, test (unit, integration with real PostgreSQL in containers, contract tests for the API, UI component tests), scan and produce versioned images; deployments to integration shall be automatic, to UAT and production by approval; releases shall be reproducible from a tag with a changelog and bill of materials.
acceptance_criteria: Given a failing test, When the pipeline runs, Then no image is published.|Given a production deployment, When requested, Then it needs an approval and records who approved.|Given a tag, When rebuilt a month later, Then the same image digest results. (edge)|Given a deployment with a migration that fails on UAT, When the pipeline runs, Then the production step is blocked. (error case)

title: Environments and infrastructure as code
requirement: All cloud environments shall be created in the company's own Azure subscriptions from infrastructure code (Azure Kubernetes Service clusters, Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Blob Storage accounts, Key Vault, Container Registry, telemetry) with the same images as the laptop stack; every Azure service is used only through a Foundation interface that also has a local implementation; environment differences are limited to configuration and secrets; the UAT environment shall mirror production topology at smaller scale; on-premises is out of scope; Azure is introduced only after the laptop stack proves the design.
acceptance_criteria: Given the infrastructure code, When applied to a fresh account, Then a working environment exists within 2 hours.|Given a manual change in production, When drift detection runs, Then it is reported. (error case)|Given UAT, When compared with production, Then only configuration and scale differ.

title: Zero-downtime deployment
requirement: API and UI deployments shall be rolling with health gates; migrations shall follow expand and contract; the worker shall drain in-flight jobs before stopping; a rollback to the previous version shall be possible within 15 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a rollout, When measured, Then no request fails due to the deployment.|Given a failed health gate, When detected, Then the rollout stops and rolls back automatically. (error case)|Given a rollback, When performed, Then the previous version serves within 15 minutes and the schema remains compatible.

title: Disaster recovery
requirement: A documented and tested plan shall restore the control plane and all tenants in a region after loss, within RTO 8 hours and RPO 15 minutes, using cross-zone replicas and off-site backups; a yearly region-level drill shall be recorded.
acceptance_criteria: Given the yearly drill, When performed, Then the control plane and a sample of tenants are restored within RTO.|Given replica lag above 60 seconds, When detected, Then an alert fires. (error case)|Given the plan, When reviewed, Then roles, steps and contacts are current within 6 months.

title: Capacity and cost management
requirement: Operators shall see capacity (connections, storage, worker utilisation, queue depth) and cost per tenant and per environment with trends and thresholds; autoscaling or scaling runbooks shall exist for each component.
acceptance_criteria: Given storage growth, When projected to exceed capacity within 30 days, Then an alert fires.|Given cost per tenant, When viewed, Then infrastructure and third-party costs are attributed by metering.|Given a scaling action, When performed, Then it is recorded with before and after capacity. (edge)|Given cost data missing for a day, When the dashboard loads, Then the gap is shown, not zero. (error case)

title: Privacy requests and personal data map
requirement: Foundation shall keep a data map of personal data fields declared by modules (purpose, retention, encryption), and provide privacy request handling: export of a person's data, correction, deletion or anonymisation (keeping business documents with the person replaced by an anonymous identifier), with a case record, due dates and audit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a deletion request for a former user, When executed, Then personal fields are anonymised across modules and documents remain with an anonymous identifier.|Given a module adds a personal field without declaring it, When the build runs, Then it fails. (error case)|Given a request opened, When 25 days pass without completion, Then an escalation is raised.

title: Consent and lawful basis records
requirement: Where consent is the basis (marketing, optional analytics), the platform shall record consent per person with version, time and source and respect withdrawal immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Given consent withdrawn, When processing runs, Then the person is excluded within one minute.|Given a consent record, When viewed, Then version, time and source are shown.|Given processing without a recorded basis, When reviewed, Then the data map flags it. (edge)|Given a consent record edited by hand, When attempted, Then it is refused; consents are append-only. (error case)

title: Sub-processor and region transparency
requirement: The platform shall publish per tenant the list of sub-processors (hosting, email, SMS, telemetry) and the data region, and notify administrators 30 days before a change.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new sub-processor, When added, Then tenants are notified 30 days before use.|Given the list requested, When viewed, Then it shows the current sub-processors and region.|Given a tenant objects, When recorded, Then the case is tracked for the account team. (edge)|Given a sub-processor change notified less than 30 days ahead, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Status page and incident communication
requirement: A public status page per region shall show component health, incidents and maintenance windows, fed by health checks and operator updates; tenants shall be able to subscribe to updates.
acceptance_criteria: Given an incident declared, When published, Then the status page updates within 5 minutes.|Given a maintenance window, When scheduled, Then subscribers are notified 7 days before.|Given health checks failing for a component, When evaluated, Then the status page shows degraded automatically. (edge)|Given a status update by a user without the operator role, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Custom fields
requirement: Tenant administrators shall add custom fields to extensible record types (text, long text, number, money, date, boolean, choice from a custom lookup, multi-choice, user, attachment, URL) with label per language, mandatory rule, validation, default, placement in a section and visibility by unit; values shall be stored in a typed, indexed structure, filterable in lists and usable in workflow conditions, exports and the API.
rationale: Carried; adds workflow and API use.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mandatory custom field, When a record is submitted without it, Then submission is refused naming the field.|Given a custom field in a filter, When a list is requested, Then results filter on it with correct paging.|Given a custom field deleted, When attempted while values exist, Then it is refused; it can be hidden instead. (error case)

title: Custom lookups
requirement: Tenant administrators shall define lookups with values (code, label per language, order, active, extra attributes), use them in custom fields and in product fields that are marked lookup-driven, and import or export them; values in use cannot be deleted, only deactivated.
acceptance_criteria: Given a value deactivated, When a new record is edited, Then it is not offered and existing records keep it.|Given a delete of a value in use, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an import of values, When run, Then duplicates by code are reported.

title: Plugin hooks
requirement: Modules shall declare hook points (before submit, after status change, on create) with payload schemas; tenant-specific logic shall attach to hook points as plugins (compiled packages loaded per tenant) or as webhook calls, with synchronous or asynchronous mode, block or pass failure policy, timeout, one active binding per hook point, and full audit of outcomes.
rationale: Carried; adds webhook-based hooks so tenants need no code for simple rules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synchronous blocking plugin that fails, When the record is submitted, Then the submission is rolled back with the plugin's message. (error case)|Given an asynchronous plugin, When the hook fires, Then the user is not blocked and the outcome is logged.|Given a plugin times out, When the policy is pass, Then processing continues and the timeout is recorded.

title: Saved views and export definitions
requirement: Users shall save personal and shared list views (columns, filters, sorts) per screen; administrators shall define export definitions (entity, columns, filters, format, schedule, destination) that run as jobs and deliver files to download or to a configured destination.
acceptance_criteria: Given a shared view published, When another user opens the screen, Then it is selectable.|Given a scheduled export, When due, Then it runs and the file is delivered.|Given a destination unreachable, When delivering, Then it retries and then alerts. (error case)

title: Unified search
requirement: Users shall search across record types by number, name and key fields with results grouped by type, filtered by permissions and policies, built on PostgreSQL full text and trigram indexes maintained by the data layer; modules declare searchable fields.
rationale: Carried quick search; adds permission filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record the user may not see, When searched, Then it is not returned.|Given a partial number, When searched, Then matching records appear ranked.|Given the index out of date, When a record changes, Then it is searchable within 10 seconds. (edge)|Given a search query over the allowed length, When sent, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Import framework
requirement: Modules shall declare import templates (columns, types, mandatory, lookups, uniqueness); the framework shall provide template download, upload (CSV, spreadsheet), validation preview with row errors, mapping of columns, dry run, execution as a job with bulk load, and a result report; imports shall respect permissions and policies like manual entry.
acceptance_criteria: Given a file with 3 invalid rows, When previewed, Then the rows and reasons are shown and the valid rows can proceed.|Given an import by a user without create permission for the entity, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a dry run, When finished, Then no data changes and the report shows what would happen.

title: Connector configuration for external systems
requirement: Integration shall provide inbound (push from ERP through the API or files) and outbound (TF-114) connector configurations with credentials in the secrets store, field mappings with transformation rules, schedules, run history, error queues and reconciliation reports. Verification and screening connectors are kinds of their own, each with one contract the modules call and a provider configured per country: identity and tax status (whether a tax or registration identifier is registered, its status, and the name it is registered to), bank account (whether an account exists and how closely its holder's name matches the one given), and sanctions (a name and country against the configured lists, answering each possible match with its list entry). Each answer keeps the provider's reference for audit.
rationale: Every enterprise customer integrates with an ERP. Verifying a supplier's identity, bank account and sanctions status is done through providers that differ by country; one contract per kind keeps the modules free of providers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an inbound file connector, When a file lands, Then it is imported through the import framework and the run recorded.|Given a mapping error, When run, Then rows land in the error queue with the reason. (error case)|Given a reconciliation report, When run, Then counts in both systems are compared and differences listed.|Given a bank account connector configured for India, When a module asks it to verify an account, Then the answer says whether the account exists and how closely the holder's name matches, with the provider's reference kept.|Given no connector of a kind configured for a country, When a module asks for that kind of check there, Then the answer says the check is not available, and the module's own rule decides what follows. (error case)
notes: Extended 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gaps G4 to G6 of the supplier management pack): the verification and screening kinds, which Supplier management's re-verification, bank verification and sanctions screening call (SUP-161, SUP-162, SUP-165). The requirements name the checks, not the providers; providers are chosen per country when the connectors are built (the pack's section 8.1). A provider that receives a supplier contact's name is a sub-processor the tenant sees (TF-198).

title: Subscription billing per user and module
requirement: The control plane shall manage plans (modules with seat prices and module fees), subscriptions per tenant (term, seats per module, start and end, renewal), subscription invoices for the SaaS itself (per period, with proration on changes), payment status, dunning steps (reminder, restriction to ReadOnly, suspension) and exports to the accounting system; transactions shall be counted and stored (TF-008) but not billed in version 1.
rationale: Decided licensing model: per number of users and per module; no transaction billing yet.
acceptance_criteria: Given 50 seats of module A and a module fee for B, When the period invoice is generated, Then it lists both with the agreed prices.|Given seats increased mid-period, When invoiced, Then the increase is prorated from the change date.|Given an unpaid invoice past the dunning steps, When evaluated, Then the tenant moves to ReadOnly and then Suspended per policy. (edge)|Given an invoice generated while seat metering is missing for part of the period, When run, Then it is held for review instead of issued. (error case)

title: AI service integration contract
requirement: The Python AI service shall access Foundation only through the public API with a service account scoped to the operations it needs, carry a correlation id, record every action as audit with actor type "AI service", and never write without a human confirmation step defined by the product; its outputs shall be stored as suggestions with confidence until confirmed.
rationale: Principle P12 and lessons from the receipt-reading feature.
acceptance_criteria: Given the AI service calls an operation outside its scope, When made, Then it is forbidden and audited. (error case)|Given a suggestion stored, When viewed, Then it is marked as suggested with confidence and the human confirmation action.|Given confirmation, When done, Then the audit shows both the AI suggestion and the human confirmation.

title: Developer documentation and ADRs
requirement: Foundation shall ship a developer guide (how to add a module, entity, permission, setting, flag, event, job, notification, custom field support, import template), architecture decision records for every "Decision" in this PRD, runbooks for operations, and API documentation generated from code; documentation shall be part of the definition of done.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new module merged without its ADR when it introduces a decision, When reviewed, Then the review is blocked.|Given the developer guide, When a new developer follows it to add an entity, Then they succeed without asking the team.|Given a runbook referenced by an alert, When opened, Then it exists and matches the current version. (edge)|Given a runbook missing for a new alert, When the alert is merged, Then the review is blocked. (error case)

title: Research-backed design and process documentation
requirement: Every functional module shall have, before design, a process reference pack: the industry process framework mapping (for procurement: APQC Process Classification Framework category 4, CIPS and ISM practice guides), applicable standards (for example Peppol BIS and UBL for business documents, UNSPSC for categories, ISO 4217, ISO 8601, UN/LOCODE, GS1 identifiers, ISO 20022 for payment status), benchmark indicators with target values, a process map (BPMN) per end-to-end process with variants and exceptions, a competitive feature review, and a research log with sources; the pack is versioned with the module and reviewed by an external practitioner before the module's first slice.
rationale: Principle P17: not limited by what the team knows today.
acceptance_criteria: Given a module starting its first slice, When the design review runs, Then the process reference pack exists and is approved, or the slice is blocked.|Given a process map, When compared with the module's state machines and requirements, Then every process step and exception maps to a requirement or a documented exclusion.|Given a standard listed as applicable, When the data model is reviewed, Then the standard's mandatory fields exist or an exclusion is recorded. (edge)|Given a pack without an external review record, When the slice starts, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Per-tenant deployment units
requirement: Provisioning shall create for each tenant a deployment unit: a namespace with network policies, API and worker container sets with resource requests and limits from the tenant's size class, configuration bound to the tenant identifier, a secrets path, a database on the deployment's server with its own role, a storage bucket with its own credentials and ingress routes for its hostnames; de-provisioning shall remove all of these in order with a retention hold on data.
rationale: Decision D-01: isolation at every technical component.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant provisioned, When inspected, Then its containers, namespace, database, bucket and secrets path exist and reference only that tenant.|Given a unit tries to reach another tenant's database or bucket, When attempted in the isolation test, Then the network policy or credentials refuse it. (error case)|Given de-provisioning, When run, Then containers and routes are removed immediately and data is deleted only after the retention hold.

title: Fleet release orchestration
requirement: The fleet orchestrator shall roll out a new application version to tenants in waves (canary tenants first, then groups by size class and region), with health gates per tenant, pause and resume, rollback per tenant, pinned versions for tenants that need a freeze, a maximum of two versions in the fleet at once, and a release record per tenant.
rationale: Many isolated units need a controlled upgrade path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release started, When the canary wave fails its health gate, Then the release pauses and no further tenants are upgraded.|Given a tenant pinned to the previous version, When the wave runs, Then it is skipped and listed as pinned.|Given a third version requested while two are in the fleet, When attempted, Then it is refused until the older version is retired. (error case)

title: Tenant database templates and cloning
requirement: Provisioning shall create tenant databases from a maintained template database at the current schema version with seeds applied, so that creation takes seconds; the orchestrator shall clone any tenant database (with data masking option) to rehearse migrations, refresh UAT from production, or investigate incidents, with every clone audited and time-limited.
rationale: Decision D-12: reduce provisioning and migration effort.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new tenant, When the database is created from the template, Then it is ready within 60 seconds at the current schema version.|Given a clone for rehearsal, When created, Then it is masked per the data map and deleted automatically after its time limit.|Given a clone requested by an operator without the permission, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Fleet migration orchestrator
requirement: The orchestrator shall apply schema migrations to tenant databases in parallel waves with a configurable concurrency, after a mandatory rehearsal on clones of representative tenants, with per-tenant status (pending, running, done, failed), automatic stop of the wave on failure rate above a threshold, resumability, drift detection between expected and actual schema version, and a report; migrations for 100 tenants shall complete within 60 minutes.
rationale: Decision D-12: migrations must not scale with manual effort.
acceptance_criteria: Given 100 tenants and concurrency 10, When the wave runs, Then all complete within 60 minutes and the report lists each tenant's duration.|Given failures above the threshold, When detected, Then the wave stops, completed tenants stay migrated, and operators are alerted. (error case)|Given drift detection, When a tenant database is behind, Then it is flagged in the fleet view before the next release.

title: Server-level backups with per-tenant restore
requirement: Backups shall run per database server (continuous archiving and daily base backup) so that backup effort does not grow with tenants; restore of a single tenant database to a point in time shall be automated (restore to a side server, extract the tenant database, swap in with verification) without affecting other tenants; backup verification shall run daily and the restore drill quarterly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a point-in-time restore of tenant A, When performed, Then tenant A is restored within 2 hours and tenant B is unaffected.|Given backup verification, When run, Then a restorable set exists for every server and a missing set alerts. (error case)|Given the quarterly drill, When performed, Then the record shows duration and result.

title: Tenant placement and density
requirement: The control plane shall assign tenants to deployments by size class and region with capacity rules (maximum tenants and total connections per database server, maximum pods per cluster), show headroom per deployment, and move a tenant to another deployment as an orchestrated job with verification and cut-over.
acceptance_criteria: Given a deployment at capacity, When a new tenant is provisioned, Then it is placed on another deployment or refused with the reason. (error case)|Given a move, When executed, Then the tenant is unavailable only during the cut-over window and all its objects exist on the target.|Given headroom, When viewed, Then connections, pods and storage per deployment are shown.

title: Cost attribution per tenant
requirement: Resource use per tenant (container CPU and memory, database size and connections, storage, egress, notifications, AI calls) shall be metered and priced with the deployment's cost model to show cost per tenant and per module, compared with its subscription revenue.
rationale: The isolated model is only sustainable with cost visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Given a month, When the cost report runs, Then every tenant shows cost and revenue with margin.|Given a tenant above its cost threshold, When evaluated, Then operators are alerted.|Given missing resource data for a day, When the report runs, Then the gap is shown, not zero. (error case)

title: Idle tenant handling
requirement: Tenant units below the small size class may scale their containers to zero after a configurable idle period and start on the first request within 30 seconds, while jobs, notifications and webhooks continue through a scheduled wake; the database stays available.
rationale: Decision O-07; cost control for very small tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Given an idle small tenant, When the first request arrives, Then the unit starts and responds within 30 seconds.|Given a scheduled job due, When the unit is idle, Then it wakes, runs the job and idles again.|Given a medium or large tenant, When idle, Then it never scales to zero. (edge)|Given a wake failure, When detected, Then an alert fires and the ingress shows a maintenance page. (error case)

title: Validation support for regulated tenants
requirement: Foundation shall support computer system validation: requirement identifiers traceable to automated tests and their results per release, release documentation (version, changes, risk assessment, test evidence), controlled configuration with versioned seeds, environment qualification records (installation verified against the infrastructure code), and a validation pack per release downloadable by tenants. The requirement identifiers of every PRD, the kernel's (TF), the business layer's (BF), the product method's (PM), the supplier portal's (SPX) and each product's prefix, are traced to tests the same way, by identifier and criterion (`REQ-012 AC2`, ADR-0041).
rationale: 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11 tenants must validate the system they use.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release, When published, Then the validation pack lists every requirement with its tests and results.|Given a requirement without a linked test, When the release pipeline runs, Then the pack flags it and the release needs an approved exception. (error case)|Given a tenant administrator, When they request the pack, Then it is downloadable from the console with the installed version.

title: Signature manifestation and audit trail review
requirement: Every signed record shall display and print the signer's full name, date and time (with timezone), and the meaning of the signature; signature records shall be linked to the record version so they cannot be copied to another record; audit trails shall be reviewable by permitted users with a periodic review record (reviewer, period, outcome); identification codes and passwords shall follow TF-012 and TF-013 with unique identifiers never reused.
rationale: 21 CFR Part 11 subparts B and C.
acceptance_criteria: Given a signed record printed, When viewed, Then the signature block shows name, time and meaning.|Given an attempt to attach a signature to another record, When made, Then it is refused because the version hash does not match. (error case)|Given a periodic audit trail review, When recorded, Then the review record lists the period and the reviewer.|Given a login identifier given to a person, When the person is deactivated or removed, Then it is never given to another person: creating a person with it is refused. (error case) (ADR-0051)
notes: AC4 added on 2026-10-23 (S3 T7, ADR-0051): the tombstone outlives the person. Built in `Iron.Kernel.Compliance` (signatures, manifestation, reviews) and `Iron.Kernel.Identity` (the identifiers); PDF output of the signature block comes with S4's document templates.

title: Organisation ownership and sharing on records
requirement: Every business record and master record shall carry an owning organisation unit and a sharing mode (private to the owner, shared with listed organisations, or global to the tenant), set by the module's rules and the user's home organisation by default; the data layer shall apply visibility filters from the user's organisation access on every list and read, and the build shall fail when a business entity lacks the owning organisation.
rationale: Decision D-13: separation by business unit is a frequent requirement in India and Asia and must exist before any product is built.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier private to organisation A, When a user of organisation B lists suppliers, Then it is not shown.|Given a global item, When any user lists items, Then it is shown.|Given a business entity without the owning organisation attribute, When the build check runs, Then it fails. (error case)

title: Organisation-scoped configuration
requirement: Settings, numbering sequences, document templates, approval configurations, notification templates, custom field visibility and feature flags shall support an organisation scope that overrides the tenant value for records owned by that organisation, resolved by the standard settings hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: Given a numbering sequence for organisation A, When a document owned by A is numbered, Then A's sequence is used.|Given no organisation override, When resolved, Then the tenant value applies.|Given an override saved by a user without the organisation's configuration permission, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Cross-organisation access
requirement: Access across organisations shall be explicit: role assignments scoped to several organisations or to a parent with children, group-level roles for consolidated views, record sharing with listed organisations, and an audit of every cross-organisation read of private records; the UI shall offer an organisation switcher and a consolidated mode for permitted users.
rationale: Group functions need to see across units without opening everything to everyone.
acceptance_criteria: Given a group finance role at the parent with children included, When listing invoices, Then invoices of all child organisations appear.|Given a user of organisation A opens a private record of B by identifier, When evaluated, Then it is refused and audited. (error case)|Given the switcher, When the user changes organisation, Then defaults (numbering, templates, visibility) follow the selected organisation.

title: Organisation lifecycle
requirement: Operators and tenant administrators shall create organisations (with a readiness checklist supplied by products), move them in the tree, merge two organisations (records reassigned with audit), split by reassigning records, and deactivate (no new records; existing records readable).
acceptance_criteria: Given a merge, When confirmed, Then all records of the merged organisation reference the survivor and the audit lists them.|Given a deactivated organisation, When a new document is created for it, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a move in the tree, When saved, Then scoped roles and settings follow.

title: Mobile companion readiness
requirement: Foundation shall prepare for a lightweight mobile companion app (approval centre and end-user expense entry): native authentication with authorization code and PKCE, refresh token rotation with device binding, push notification channel with device registration, compact API operations for queues and actions with idempotency keys, offline-tolerant action submission, and mobile telemetry; the app itself is a later slice.
acceptance_criteria: Given a native client, When it authenticates with PKCE, Then it receives tokens bound to the device and can refresh.|Given an approval action submitted twice after a network retry, When processed, Then one decision is recorded.|Given a device registered for push, When an approval is due, Then a push notification is sent and recorded as a delivery.|Given a revoked device, When it tries to refresh, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Technology for the app to be decided (O-05).

title: Horizontal scaling of one tenant unit
requirement: A tenant unit's API and worker container sets shall scale horizontally by configuration and by load (CPU, request latency, queue depth), with stateless API nodes, server-side sessions in the database or a shared cache so that no node affinity is needed, worker partitioning of queued work, and real-time connections backed by a shared backplane when more than one API node exists.
rationale: Principle P15; a global enterprise tenant needs many nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Given latency above target, When autoscaling evaluates, Then API replicas increase within 2 minutes and latency returns to target.|Given two API nodes, When a user's requests land on different nodes, Then the session and real-time updates work unchanged.|Given a worker node failure, When detected, Then its in-flight jobs are retried on other nodes without duplication. (error case)

title: Database scaling for a large tenant
requirement: The data layer shall support, by configuration and without code change in products: connection pooling per unit, read replicas for reporting and for list queries marked read-only, table partitioning for the largest tables (by organisation or by period) with partition maintenance jobs, archival of closed documents to cheaper storage with on-demand recall, and index and statistics maintenance; schema conventions shall forbid patterns that prevent partitioning (for example unique constraints without the partition key).
acceptance_criteria: Given a reporting query marked read-only, When executed, Then it runs on a replica and replica lag is visible in telemetry.|Given a partitioned table, When a new period starts, Then its partition exists before the first row (maintenance job) and queries by period use only the relevant partitions.|Given a module adds a unique constraint without the partition key on a partitioned table, When the schema check runs, Then it fails. (error case)

title: Dedicated deployment for a tenant
