requirement: The control plane shall provision a dedicated deployment (own cluster, own database server, own storage account, own telemetry and secrets) for a tenant that requires it, run by the same fleet tooling and images, with the tenant's region, size and compliance options recorded; moving a tenant from a shared deployment to a dedicated one shall be an orchestrated migration with verification and a planned cut-over.
rationale: Decision D-15: dedicated infrastructure must be an option.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dedicated deployment requested, When provisioned, Then the tenant runs there with the same version as the fleet and appears in the fleet view as dedicated.|Given a move from shared to dedicated, When executed, Then data, files and secrets are migrated, verified and cut over within the planned window, and the shared copy is deleted after confirmation.|Given a dedicated deployment missing a required component, When provisioning runs, Then it stops and reports the component. (error case)

title: Load and capacity testing harness
requirement: Foundation shall ship a load test pack (scenario per module, data generator for large tenants, realistic think times) runnable on the laptop at small scale and on a dedicated deployment at the largest-tenant targets of section 5, with results stored per release and regression alerts on latency or throughput loss above 10 percent.
rationale: Scale claims need proof on every release.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release, When the laptop-scale load test runs in the pipeline, Then results are stored and compared with the previous release.|Given a regression above 10 percent, When detected, Then the release is blocked until reviewed. (error case)|Given the dedicated deployment, When the full-scale test runs, Then the section 5 targets are met or the gaps are listed.

title: Multi-region readiness
requirement: The design shall allow a second region later without rework: region recorded on every tenant and deployment, one control plane per region, no cross-region database joins, region-aware object storage and backups, and a documented plan for linking a supplier identity across regions.
rationale: Global enterprises operate in several regions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a second region added in a test, When a tenant is created there, Then it is provisioned by that region's control plane and served there.|Given a request for a tenant of another region, When it arrives at the wrong region's ingress, Then it is redirected, not served. (error case)|Given the architecture review, When checked, Then no component holds cross-region state except the documented supplier identity link.

title: Supplier Network identity
requirement: Supplier users shall register once in the Supplier Network with email verification, password policy and MFA as in TF-011 to TF-013, belong to one supplier organisation (roles: primary contact, contact), and log in to one portal for all customers; tenants shall never store supplier credentials; supplier SSO is a later slice.
rationale: Decision D-19: one portal for all suppliers of all tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier user with relationships to customers A and B, When they log in once, Then they see both customers' items.|Given a tenant tries to create a supplier credential, When attempted, Then it is refused; it creates an invitation instead. (error case)|Given MFA required by any connected customer, When the user logs in, Then MFA is enforced for the whole session.

title: Supplier organisation registry
requirement: The network shall hold supplier organisations with legal name, country, tax identifiers (with a verified flag), addresses, contacts, bank accounts (encrypted), documents with expiry and a public profile; the supplier maintains this master copy; duplicate organisations shall be detected on registration; a tenant invitation shall match an existing organisation by tax identifier or email domain before creating a new one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant invites a supplier whose tax identifier exists in the network, When the invitation is sent, Then it targets the existing organisation.|Given two organisations with the same verified tax identifier, When the second registers, Then it is flagged as a duplicate and blocked until resolved. (error case)|Given a profile change by the supplier, When saved, Then it is versioned and offered to connected tenants (TF-235).

title: Relationships and invitations
requirement: A relationship between a supplier organisation and a tenant shall have states Invited, Connected, OnHold, Ended; a tenant creates it by inviting (email or network identifier) with its own supplier record identifier; the supplier accepts or declines; either side may end it; a tenant sees only its own relationships; the supplier sees all of theirs.
acceptance_criteria: Given an invitation accepted, When the relationship is Connected, Then the tenant's supplier record is linked to the network organisation and the supplier's inbox starts receiving that tenant's items.|Given tenant A queries relationships, When executed, Then tenant B's relationships are never returned. (error case)|Given a relationship ended by the tenant, When the supplier opens the portal, Then that customer's items are read-only history.

title: Action index and inbox
requirement: Tenant units shall push index events (create, update, close) for supplier-relevant items with a minimal, tenant-configurable field set (tenant, organisation, document type, identifier, number, status, amount, currency, due date, link); the network shall keep one inbox per supplier organisation across all customers with filters by customer, type, status and due date, bulk selection, and shall never store document content; the index for a tenant shall be rebuildable from the tenant on demand and reconciled nightly.
rationale: The supplier's single view across customers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an order issued in tenant A, When the event arrives, Then the inbox shows it within 10 seconds with the configured fields.|Given a tenant removes the amount field from its index configuration, When new events arrive, Then amounts are absent for that tenant.|Given a rebuild requested, When run, Then the index for that tenant matches the tenant's open items and differences are reported. (error case)

title: Delegated access to tenant units
requirement: When a supplier user opens or acts on a customer's document, the network shall exchange the user's session for a short-lived token scoped to that tenant, that relationship and the supplier role, call the tenant unit's API with it, and the tenant unit shall enforce its own permissions and ownership policies and audit the supplier user, the relationship and the network as caller; tokens shall not be reusable across tenants or relationships.
rationale: Business data and rules stay in the tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Given a token for tenant A, When used against tenant B, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an acknowledgement submitted through the network, When audited in the tenant, Then the supplier user, relationship and network caller are recorded.|Given a relationship on hold, When a token is requested for it, Then it is refused and the inbox shows the hold.

title: Profile propagation and acceptance
requirement: Changes to the supplier's master profile shall be offered to each connected tenant as proposed changes; each tenant applies its own approval and verification rules (for example bank verification) before accepting; a tenant may decline; the supplier sees the acceptance status per customer; tenants may keep tenant-specific values that the network never overwrites.
rationale: One maintenance point for the supplier, full control for each customer.
acceptance_criteria: Given a changed bank account in the network, When offered to tenants A and B, Then each sees a pending change with its own verification checklist.|Given tenant A declines, When viewed by the supplier, Then the status shows declined for A and accepted for B.|Given a tenant-specific payment term, When the network profile changes, Then the term is unchanged. (edge)|Given a propagation message that fails validation in the tenant, When received, Then it is rejected with the reason and shown to the supplier. (error case)

title: Cross-customer operations for suppliers
requirement: The portal shall let a supplier user act efficiently across customers: a unified inbox, bulk acknowledgement of orders across customers (each executed in its tenant), a customer switcher that filters all screens, one notification digest across customers, saved views, and exports of their own documents index per customer.
acceptance_criteria: Given five orders from three customers selected, When bulk acknowledged, Then each is acknowledged in its tenant and per-item results are shown.|Given one tenant unreachable, When the bulk action runs, Then the other items succeed and the failed ones are listed for retry. (error case)|Given the daily digest chosen, When items arrive from several customers, Then one email lists them grouped by customer.

title: Network isolation and data minimisation
requirement: The network shall hold only supplier-owned data and the minimal action index; tenants shall not see other tenants' relationships, indexes or configurations; index fields shall be configurable per tenant with a minimal default; index data shall follow the tenant's retention; supplier personal data shall follow privacy requirements; the network shall have its own audit, its own SLO and its own evidence pack.
rationale: Compliance for a multi-tenant plane next to isolated units.
acceptance_criteria: Given the cross-tenant test suite run against the network, When executed, Then no tenant can read another tenant's relationship or index.|Given a tenant decommissioned, When processed, Then its index and relationships are removed within the retention hold.|Given a request for document content from the network database, When made, Then none exists by design (schema check). (error case)

title: Network availability and decoupling
requirement: The network and tenant units shall fail independently: tenant units queue index events in their outbox when the network is down; the portal shows the index and marks a tenant as unreachable when its unit is down; the network runs in at least two availability zones with its own backups and SLO (99.9 percent).
rationale: One portal must not become a single point of failure.
acceptance_criteria: Given the network down for an hour, When it returns, Then queued index events are delivered in order and the inbox is complete.|Given tenant A's unit down, When the supplier opens the inbox, Then A's items are shown as unreachable and B's items open normally. (error case)|Given a network zone failure, When it happens, Then the portal continues from the other zone.

title: Network console and supplier support
requirement: Operators shall manage the network (supplier organisations, duplicates, relationships, index health, unreachable tenants, supplier support cases) in a console; tenant buyers shall see only their relationships and may impersonate a supplier user within their tenant's scope only, with network audit; supplier primary contacts shall manage their own users.
rationale: Operations and support of the shared plane.
acceptance_criteria: Given a duplicate organisation flagged, When an operator merges, Then relationships and users move to the survivor and the audit lists them.|Given a tenant buyer impersonates a supplier user, When they try to open another customer's item, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a supplier primary contact, When they add a user, Then the user can log in with access to all the organisation's customers per role.

title: Content visibility and visibility tags
requirement: Visibility tags shall narrow what a person sees, by six rules: (1) administrators define the visibility tags; (2) master data and transactions can carry tags, and a record without tags is visible to everyone who passes roles and units; (3) a person can hold tags, and a person without tags sees every record; (4) a person sees a tagged record when they share at least one tag with it; (5) a person can only put tags they hold on a record; (6) transactions may take their tags from their master, and each product says how. The filter applies after roles, permissions and units, inside the same query, and only narrows (ADR-0032); changes of tags on records and on people are audited; the access explanation shows the tags as a check (ADR-0039); access reviews cover who holds which tags.
rationale: Carried: the current product's content groups. Roles and units decide what a person may do and where; tags decide which of those records they see, without a unit or a role for every region, programme or category.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record tagged APAC and LATAM and a person holding only APAC, When the person lists the records, Then the record is shown (rule 4).|Given a record tagged LATAM and a person holding only APAC, When the person opens it by identifier, Then it answers not found, and the explanation of the person's access names the tag check. (error case)|Given a record without tags, When a person who passes roles and units lists the records, Then it is shown (rule 2).|Given a person who holds no tags, When they list records they pass roles and units for, Then tagged and untagged records are shown (rule 3).|Given a person holding only APAC, When they put LATAM on a record, Then it is refused naming the tag (rule 5). (error case)|Given 100 records of which the person may see 40 by their tags, When the list is paged, Then the total and the pages count the 40.|Given a tag added to a person or a record, When saved, Then the audit records the change with before and after, and the next access review lists the person's tags.|Given a transaction created from a master with tags and a product rule that the transaction takes them, When it is saved, Then it carries the master's tags (rule 6).
notes: Also called content groups, the current product's name. Scheduled before the first business slice (section 7), because every business record type needs it from its first day. The Business PRD says which masters carry tags (its section 5.10); each product says how its transactions take theirs (its section 10).

title: Approvals, tasks and notifications respect access
requirement: An approval step, a task or a notification shall go only to a person who can read the record it concerns, by scope, record policy and visibility tags; a configured approver who cannot read the record is reported as a configuration error and the approval configuration's fallback applies (TF-091); a notification never contains data its reader may not read.
rationale: Organisation separation and visibility tags would mean little if an approval, a task or an email showed a record to someone the record's own page refuses. The archived Functional Foundation PRD asked it for organisations (its FF-184).
acceptance_criteria: Given an approval configuration whose approver has no scope over the record's unit, When the chain is built, Then the step is not given to that approver, a configuration error names the configuration, the step and the approver, and the configuration's fallback applies. (error case)|Given a task about a record its intended assignee cannot read, When it is assigned, Then it is refused naming the missing access. (error case)|Given a daily digest that would list a record tagged LATAM for a reader holding only APAC, When the digest is built, Then that record is left out.|Given an approver who can read the record, When the chain is built, Then the step is given to them as configured.
notes: Written at the PRD split's checkpoint, the design session's answer to FF-184's clause that approvals, tasks and notifications respect the same access (`../requirements-map.md`).

title: Forms engine
requirement: The kernel shall provide forms: form templates with sections, questions of typed answers, validation, conditional questions, scoring and weights, and versions; attachments with typed metadata, an issue date and an expiry date among them; instances of a template attached to a record; sections that name their own reviewers and are approved or returned on their own, a returned section going back to the respondent with comments per question while the others wait; answers pre-filled from the record (TF-245); responses audited, with an optional electronic signature (TF-063); and every response kept as a version, with a comparison of any two versions of the same instance's responses. Supplier information collection, onboarding forms, surveys and sourcing evaluations use it.
rationale: Four products need structured questions with answers that can be scored and signed; one engine keeps them alike and saves building it four times. Supplier information collection also needs evidence with its validity, review by the team each section belongs to (finance for financial statements, quality for certificates), and this year's answers set against last year's.
acceptance_criteria: Given a question shown only when an earlier answer is yes, When the earlier answer is no, Then the question is hidden and not required.|Given a required number question answered with text, When the response is submitted, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)|Given a template with scored questions and weights, When a response is scored, Then its score is the weighted sum and is stored with the response.|Given a template changed after an instance was sent, When the instance is opened, Then it shows the version it was sent with.|Given a template that requires a signature, When a response is submitted without the re-authentication the tenant requires, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a response submitted, When the audit is searched for its record, Then the submitter, the time and the answers are there.|Given a question that asks for a certificate with its issue and expiry dates, When a response is submitted with an expiry date before the issue date, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)|Given a template whose financial section names the finance reviewers, When a response is submitted, Then that section waits for a finance reviewer's decision, and each section's decision is recorded with its reviewer and time.|Given a section returned with a comment on one question, When the respondent opens the response, Then only that section can be edited, the comment shows beside its question, and the other sections keep their decisions.|Given a person who is not among a section's reviewers, When they approve that section, Then it is refused naming the section. (error case)|Given last year's and this year's responses to the same recurring instance, When they are compared, Then each changed answer is listed with both values, and unchanged answers are not.
notes: Decided 2026-10-20: built in S4, before supplier questionnaires (SUP-042, replaced by supplier information collection, SUP-221 to SUP-231, on 2026-10-21) and onboarding forms (SUP-002) need it; surveys and sourcing come later. Its module is `Iron.Kernel.Forms` (section 2.1). Extended 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the supplier management pack's section 8.4): attachments with issue and expiry dates, section reviewers and decisions per section, pre-fill, and versions of responses with their comparison (AC7 to AC11).

title: Mapping form answers to records
requirement: A module shall declare which fields of its records are mappable (a field of a master record, a document type of its own, a custom field, TF-200), each with its type; a form question may map to one mappable field. When an instance is sent for a record, each mapped question is pre-filled with the field's current value, and the respondent confirms it or changes it. A mapped answer is never written to the record by the forms engine: when the response is approved, each changed mapped answer is handed to the module that owns the field as a change proposal (the field, its value when the instance was sent, the new value, and the response as source and evidence), and that module decides what happens, under its own rules, approvals and verification.
rationale: Forms collect what records already hold. Without mapping, a reviewer retypes approved answers into the record, with mistakes; with direct writes, a form would bypass the owning module's approvals and verification, and a bank account from a questionnaire would reach a payment unchecked.
acceptance_criteria: Given a question mapped to a supplier's website and a supplier whose record holds a website, When the instance is sent, Then the question shows the current website pre-filled.|Given a mapped answer the respondent changed, When the response is approved, Then the owning module receives one change proposal with the field, the value when sent, the new value and the response, and the record is unchanged until the module applies it.|Given a mapped answer confirmed unchanged, When the response is approved, Then no change proposal is made for it.|Given a question mapped to a field its module has not declared mappable, When the template is saved, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)|Given an answer whose type does not fit its field (text for a date), When the response is submitted, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)|Given a change proposal the owning module refuses (its module switched off for the tenant), When the response is approved, Then the response stays approved, the proposal is recorded as refused with the module's reason, and the reviewers are told. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the supplier management pack's section 8.4). Built in S4 with the forms engine. Its first user is supplier information collection, whose change proposals become supplier change requests on the governed changes of TF-247 (SUP-227); the forms engine knows nothing of governed changes, so it can ship before them (section 7.1). Templates, responses, sections and their versions are the forms engine's; the requests that target records are the product's (the pack's section 8.5, decision 6).

title: One-time verified access for external respondents
requirement: A module shall be able to send a one-time verified link to an external contact it already knows, for one purpose: answering one form instance, or accepting one invitation. The link names its purpose and its contact; opening it asks for a code sent to that contact's email address, valid for 10 minutes; a verified link opens its purpose and nothing else, holds no session beyond it, ends when its purpose is submitted or when it expires (14 days after it was sent, unless the module sets less), and locks for an hour after five wrong codes. Every send, opening, code check and submission is audited with the contact's address, and the module that sent the link may revoke it at any time.
rationale: Some suppliers answer one questionnaire a year and will never work in a portal; asking them to register first slows every collection and onboarding. A link that proves who opens it, does one thing and then ends, lets them answer safely, and lets supplier information collection run before the Supplier Network exists (S8).
acceptance_criteria: Given a link sent to a supplier contact for one information request, When the contact opens it and enters the emailed code, Then the request's form opens, and only that form.|Given a verified link, When its holder asks for any other form, record, file or page of the tenant, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a link past its expiry, or one whose form was submitted, When it is opened, Then it is refused, saying the sender can send a new link. (error case)|Given five wrong codes within an hour, When a sixth is entered, Then the link is locked for an hour and the sender is told. (error case)|Given an email address that is not a contact on the record the link is for, When a module asks to send a link to it, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a link revoked by the module that sent it, When it is opened, Then it is refused.|Given a link that was used, When the audit is searched for it, Then its send, its opening, every code check and its submission are there, each with the contact's address and the time.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G13 of the supplier management pack). Built in S4 with the forms engine; its part is `Iron.Kernel.Identity`'s, beside invitations (section 2.1). It is not a login: no password, no session beyond its purpose, and the Supplier Network (TF-230) stays the way a supplier works. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: the code's validity (10 minutes), the link's validity (14 days at most) and the lock after five wrong codes in an hour are the defaults. What a module does with what arrives this way is the module's: Supplier management still verifies a critical field out of band (SUP-205, SPX-008).

title: Governed changes to records
requirement: The kernel shall govern changes to the records a module registers. A change is a change request: the record, its source, who asked, a reason, evidence, an effective date, and field-level changes, each with its old and its new value. The module declares a class for each field of a governed entity, uncontrolled, controlled or critical, and a floor below which a tenant may not lower it; the tenant may raise a class. Uncontrolled changes apply at once and are recorded. Controlled and critical changes are routed through the workflow engine (TF-090) by the approval configuration of the module's document type, and decided field by field: approve, reject with a reason, or return a question to the requester; a request may end partly applied. Nobody decides a change they requested (TF-036). An approved change applies on its effective date, by a job, and only when each field's old value is still the current value; otherwise that field stops and returns to review. A field has at most one pending change; a second waits for the first to end. The module adds its own steps through hooks: a verification that must pass before a critical field applies, the notifications after a change applies, and the impact preview of the documents that use the values. Every applied change is in the field-level history (TF-062) with its request.
rationale: Every master needs controlled change: suppliers first, then items, legal entities, people, and the records of later suites. One mechanism keeps the rules alike (approval, segregation, effective dates, concurrency, history), and each module adds only what is its own. A change written straight to a record, by a person, an import or a form, is how bank fraud and silent master-data errors begin.
acceptance_criteria: Given a change request with an uncontrolled and a controlled field, When it is submitted, Then the uncontrolled field applies at once and is in the history, and the controlled field waits for approval.|Given one field approved and another rejected with a reason, When the decisions are recorded, Then the first applies, the second does not, and the requester sees both outcomes with the reason.|Given a change requested by a person, When the same person approves it, Then it is refused naming the segregation rule. (error case)|Given an approved change effective on the first of next month, When that day comes, Then the job applies it, and until then the record keeps its current value.|Given a change whose old value is no longer the record's value when it comes to apply, When the job runs, Then that field is not applied and returns to review, naming the field and both values. (error case)|Given a pending change to a field, When a second change to the same field is submitted, Then it waits until the first ends, and the requester is told why.|Given a module's verification hook on a critical field, When the change is approved, Then it applies only after the hook reports success, and a failed verification leaves the record unchanged with the reason on the request. (error case)|Given a tenant that lowers a field below its module's floor (a critical field to controlled), When the classes are saved, Then it is refused naming the field and its floor. (error case)|Given an applied change, When the record's history is opened, Then the field, the old and new values, the source, the requester, the deciders and the effective date are shown.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the supplier management pack's sections 8.2, 8.4 and 8.5). Built in S5, after the workflow engine; its module is `Iron.Kernel.Changes` (section 2.1). Supplier management is its first user (SUP-201 to SUP-211) and adds through hooks only what is a supplier's own: bank verification, the cooling period, and the announcement to the contacts known before a change (ADR-0043, decision 8). No version tables: a record holds its current values, a future-dated change waits as an approved request, and history is TF-062's (the pack's section 8.5, decision 2). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a module sets a floor per field and a tenant may raise a class but never lower it below the floor.
